blocks.title: Thresholded armwise Moore--Penrose inverse
blocks.body: Let \(s=(M_0(s),M_1(s),N_0(s),N_1(s),m_X(s))\) be an observable summary and put \(s_0:=\pi_0\sigma_0^2\). For \(t\in\{0,1\}\), write a real singular-value expansion \(M_t(s)=\sum_j \sigma_j u_jv_j^\top\), with \(\sigma_j\ge0\). The thresholded Moore--Penrose inverse of the armwise proxy moment is\[ (M_t(s))^\dagger_{\ge s_0/2}:=\sum_{\sigma_j\ge s_0/2}\sigma_j^{-1}v_ju_j^\top.\]

blocks.title: Finite transport-plan relation
blocks.body: Let \(\nu=\sum_{a=1}^r w_a\delta_{x_a}\) and \(\widehat\lambda_n=\sum_{b=1}^{\widehat r}\widehat w_b\delta_{\widehat x_b}\) be finite probability laws on \([-L_\tau,L_\tau]\). We write \(\gamma:\nu\leadsto\widehat\lambda_n\) when \(\gamma=(\gamma_{ab})_{1\le a\le r,\,1\le b\le\widehat r}\) is a finite transport plan with \(\gamma_{ab}\ge0\), \(\sum_{b=1}^{\widehat r}\gamma_{ab}=w_a\) for every \(a\), and \(\sum_{a=1}^{r}\gamma_{ab}=\widehat w_b\) for every \(b\). Its absolute-distance transport cost is \(\sum_{a=1}^{r}\sum_{b=1}^{\widehat r}\gamma_{ab}|x_a-\widehat x_b|\).

blocks.title: VMW Assumption 4
blocks.body:
For a one-unit full-data law \(P\), VMW Assumption 4 holds when \(0<k\), \(k\le d_x\), \(k\le d_z\), and there exist positive constants \(L_X,L_{ZX},L_{YZX},\pi,\sigma\) such that \(\|X\|_2\le L_X\), \(\|ZX^\top\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le L_{ZX}\), and \(\|YZX^\top\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le L_{YZX}\) almost surely under \(P\), both treatment-arm probabilities satisfy \(P(T=t)\ge\pi\) for \(t\in\{0,1\}\), and there is a population top-\(k\) right singular basis \(V\) of the stacked proxy moment \([M_0(P);M_1(P)]\) for which
\[
\sigma_k([M_0(P);M_1(P)])\ge\sigma,
\qquad
\sigma_k(M_t(P)V)\ge\sigma\quad\text{for }t\in\{0,1\}.
\]

blocks.title: Summary radius \(r_{n,\alpha}\)
blocks.body:
For sample size \(n\), miscoverage level \(\alpha\), concentration constant \(C_0\), and envelope constant \(L\), the simultaneous summary radius is
\[
r_{n,\alpha}:=C_0L\sqrt{\frac{\log(C_0/\alpha)}{n}}.
\]
This is the radius used in the event \(E_P=\{d_S(\widehat S_n,S(P))\le r_{n,\alpha}\}\).

blocks.title: Endpoint feasibility for cluster-mass extrema
blocks.body: For confidence-set data with atom floor \(m_\star\), outer radius \(R_{n,\alpha}\), computed center \(\widehat\lambda_n\), association radius \(\rho_{n,\alpha}\), empirical component \(C\), and candidate endpoint value \(m\), say that \(\operatorname{EndpointFeasible}(C,m)\) holds when there exists a law \(\xi\in\mathcal P_{\le k,m_\star}([-L_\tau,L_\tau])\) and a transport plan \(\gamma\) from \(\xi\) to \(\widehat\lambda_n\) such that \[ \sum_{a,b}\gamma_{ab}|x_a-\widehat x_b|\le R_{n,\alpha} \] and \[ m=\xi(K_C(\xi)),\qquad K_C(\xi):=\{x\in\operatorname{supp}(\xi):\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\le\rho_{n,\alpha}\}. \] Thus the lower and upper endpoints of \(I_C\) are the infimum and supremum of feasible values \(m\) over the same ordered-support, atom-floor, simplex, and transport constraints.

blocks.title: Atomic measure \(\nu_\xi\)
blocks.body:
For a represented atomic record \(\xi=((w_i)_{i<k},(a_i)_{i<k})\), define
\[
\nu_\xi=\sum_{i<k}\max\{w_i,0\}\,\delta_{a_i}.
\]
Repeated labelled locations contribute additively through the nonnegative masses \(\max\{w_i,0\}\).

blocks.title: Candidate count \(N_A\)
blocks.body:
For a prescribed structured-lattice estimator \(A\), let
\[
N_A\in\mathbb N
\]
be the cardinality of its finite exhaustive candidate list. The listed candidates are indexed as
\[
\vartheta_i=(V_i,R_i,p_i,\tau_i),
\qquad i=1,\ldots,N_A,
\]
and this enumeration is the duplicate-free lexicographically ordered list of all well-formed structured lattice points at the stated sample size, conditioning constants, and effect-support radius.

blocks.title: Matrix action operator
blocks.body:
For \(r,c\in\mathbb N\) and any real \(r\times c\) matrix \(A\), the associated continuous linear operator from \(\mathbb R^c\) to \(\mathbb R^r\) is the ordinary finite-dimensional matrix action:
\[
x\longmapsto Ax .
\]

blocks.title: Thresholded empirical compressed operator
blocks.body: For a rectangular matrix \(G=\sum_j\sigma_j u_jv_j^\top\), define the thresholded pseudoinverse \[G^\dagger_{\ge s_0/2}:=\sum_{\sigma_j\ge s_0/2}\sigma_j^{-1}v_ju_j^\top.\] The empirical compressed operator is \[\widehat D_n:=(\widehat M_{1,n})^\dagger_{\ge s_0/2}\widehat N_{1,n}-(\widehat M_{0,n})^\dagger_{\ge s_0/2}\widehat N_{0,n}.\]

blocks.title: Structured comparison operator
blocks.body:
For a structured lattice point \(\vartheta=(V,R,p,\tau)\), define the structured comparison operator by
\[
\operatorname{Op}(\vartheta):=VR^{-1}\operatorname{diag}(\tau)RV^\top .
\]
For an empirical summary \(s=(M_0,M_1,N_0,N_1,m_X)\) and threshold \(s_0/2=\pi_0\sigma_0^2/2\), define the empirical comparison operator by
\[
\widehat{\operatorname{Op}}(s):=M_{1,\ge s_0/2}^{\dagger}N_1-M_{0,\ge s_0/2}^{\dagger}N_0,
\]
where \(M_{t,\ge s_0/2}^{\dagger}\) is the singular-value-thresholded pseudoinverse retaining singular directions with singular value at least \(s_0/2\). In the lattice criterion, these operators are compared through
\[
\|\operatorname{Op}(\vartheta)-\widehat{\operatorname{Op}}(\widehat S_n)\|_{\mathrm{op}}.
\]

blocks.title: Matrix operator norm \(\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\)
blocks.body:
For natural numbers \(r\) and \(c\) and a real \(r\times c\) matrix \(A\), \(A\) acts as the ordinary finite-dimensional linear map
\[
x\mapsto Ax,
\qquad x\in\mathbb R^c.
\]
Its Euclidean operator norm is
\[
\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}:=\sup_{\|x\|_2\le 1}\|Ax\|_2.
\]
Thus comparisons of matrix-valued operators use the ordinary matrix operator norm, for example
\[
\|\operatorname{Op}(\vartheta)-\widehat{\operatorname{Op}}(\widehat S_n)\|_{\mathrm{op}}.
\]

blocks.title: Quotient atomic law structure
blocks.body:
For every \(k\in\mathbb N\) and \(r\in\mathbb R\), consider the quotient of valid labelled at-most-\(k\)-atomic probability laws supported in the radius-\(r\) interval by equality of their induced measures.  For a quotient law \(
u\) in this space, \(\operatorname{representative}(
u)\) is the noncomputably chosen valid labelled representative of the equivalence class \(
u\).

The topology on this quotient space is the topology coinduced by the canonical quotient map from valid labelled laws to their induced-measure equivalence classes.  Its measurable structure is the mapped measurable structure along the same quotient map.  With this coinduced topology, the quotient space is compact.

blocks.title: Structured lattice candidate spaces
blocks.body: Put \(m_\star:=\pi_0\), \(s_0:=\pi_0\sigma_0^2\), \[H_n:=\lceil\sqrt n\rceil+\lceil\pi_0^{-1}\rceil+2k+\lceil4\sqrt{d_xk}\rceil+\lceil2k/\sigma_0\rceil,\qquad q_n:=H_n^{-1},\] and \(\ell_n:=\lceil m_\star H_n\rceil\). Let \(\mathcal V_n\) consist of the polar factors \(G(G^\top G)^{-1/2}\) of all \(G\in(q_n\mathbb Z)^{d_x\times k}\) satisfying \(|G_{ij}|\le1\) and \(\sigma_k(G)\ge1/2\). Let \(\mathcal R_n\) consist of all \(R\in(q_n\mathbb Z)^{k\times k}\) satisfying \(\sigma_k(R)\ge\sigma_0/2\) and \(\lVert R\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le2\sqrt{k}L\). Define \[\mathcal P_n:=\left\{H_n^{-1}(a_1,\ldots,a_k)^\top:a_u\in\{\ell_n,\ldots,H_n\},\ \sum_{u=1}^k a_u=H_n\right\},\] and let \(\mathcal T_n\) be the \(k\)-fold product of the clipped \(q_n\)-lattice in \([-L_\tau,L_\tau]\).

blocks.title: Lattice-implied operator and quotient law
blocks.body: For \(\vartheta=(V,R,p,\tau)\in\mathcal V_n\times\mathcal R_n\times\mathcal P_n\times\mathcal T_n\), define \[D_\vartheta:=VR^{-1}\operatorname{diag}(\tau)RV^\top,\qquad m_\vartheta:=VR^\top p,\qquad b_\vartheta:=RV^\top e_1,\] and define the associated quotient law by \[\lambda_\vartheta:=\sum_{u=1}^k p_u\delta_{\tau_u}.\]

blocks.title: All-ones vector $\mathbf 1_k$
blocks.body: The vector $\mathbf 1_k\in\mathbb R^k$ is the all-ones vector, with coordinate $(\mathbf 1_k)_u=1$ for every latent-coordinate index $u=1,\ldots,k$.

blocks.title: Structured-lattice objective $J_n(\vartheta;s)$
blocks.body:
Put $s_0:=\pi_0\sigma_0^2$. For a summary $s=(M_0,M_1,N_0,N_1,m_X)\in(\mathbb R^{d_z\times d_x})^4\times\mathbb R^{d_x}$, define the thresholded pseudoinverse by writing a rectangular matrix $G=\sum_j\sigma_j u_jv_j^\top$ and setting $G^\dagger_{\ge s_0/2}:=\sum_{\sigma_j\ge s_0/2}\sigma_j^{-1}v_ju_j^\top$. Set $\widehat D(s):=M_1^\dagger{}_{\ge s_0/2}N_1-M_0^\dagger{}_{\ge s_0/2}N_0$. For $\vartheta=(V,R,p,\tau)\in\mathcal V_n\times\mathcal R_n\times\mathcal P_n\times\mathcal T_n$, with $V\in\mathbb R^{d_x\times k}$, $R\in\mathbb R^{k\times k}$ invertible on $\mathcal R_n$, $p\in\Delta^{k-1}$, and $\tau\in[-L_\tau,L_\tau]^k$, define $D_\vartheta:=VR^{-1}\operatorname{diag}(\tau)RV^\top$, $m_\vartheta:=VR^\top p$, $b_\vartheta:=RV^\top e_1$, and $\lambda_\vartheta:=\sum_{u=1}^kp_u\delta_{\tau_u}$. The structured-lattice criterion at summary $s$ is 
\[
J_n(\vartheta;s):=\lVert D_\vartheta-\widehat D(s)\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}+\lVert m_\vartheta-m_X\rVert_2+\lVert b_\vartheta-\mathbf 1_k\rVert_2.
\]
For the empirical summary $\widehat S_n$, write $J_n(\vartheta):=J_n(\vartheta;\widehat S_n)$.

blocks.title: Operation count for the structured-lattice estimator
blocks.body: For the structured-lattice estimator \(\widehat\lambda_n\), let \(\mathcal A_n:=\mathcal V_n\times\mathcal R_n\times\mathcal P_n\times\mathcal T_n\) denote its lexicographically ordered finite candidate list. In the fixed-dimensional unit-cost exact-real model, define\[\operatorname{ops}(\widehat\lambda_n):=n+\#\mathcal A_n.\]The term \(n\) counts formation of the empirical summary \(\widehat S_n\), and \(\#\mathcal A_n\) counts exhaustive evaluation of the fixed-dimensional objective \(J_n(\vartheta)\) once for each \(\vartheta\in\mathcal A_n\), including the fixed-size arithmetic, comparison, singular-value, polar-decomposition, and root-isolation operations used by that candidate evaluation.

blocks.title: Observed-record space \(O_{d_x,d_z}\)
blocks.body:
Write \(O_{d_x,d_z}\) for the observed-record space of quadruples
\[
O=(T,X,Z,Y),
\]
where \(T\in\{0,1\}\), \(X\in\mathbb R^{d_x}\), \(Z\in\mathbb R^{d_z}\), and \(Y\in\mathbb R\).

blocks.title: Wasserstein distance \(W_1(\nu,\xi)\)
blocks.body:
For represented atomic laws
\[
\nu=\sum_i p_i\delta_{x_i},
\qquad
\xi=\sum_j q_j\delta_{y_j},
\]
define \(W_1(\nu,\xi)\) by
\[
W_1(\nu,\xi)
=
\min_{\gamma_{ij}\ge 0}
\sum_{i,j}\gamma_{ij}|x_i-y_j|,
\]
where the minimum is over all nonnegative couplings \((\gamma_{ij})_{i,j}\) whose marginals are the represented masses:
\[
\sum_j \gamma_{ij}=p_i
\quad\text{for every }i,
\qquad
\sum_i \gamma_{ij}=q_j
\quad\text{for every }j.
\]

blocks.title: Observed-data marginal \(P_O\)
blocks.body:
For a full-data probability law \(P\), let
\[
O=(T,X,Z,Y)
\]
be the observed record. The observed-data marginal of \(P\) is
\[
P_O:=P\circ O^{-1}.
\]

blocks.title: Latent-class mass \(p_u\)
blocks.body:
For each latent class \(u\), its latent-class mass is
\[
p_u:=P(U=u).
\]

blocks.title: Latent conditional mean \(\mu_{tu}\)
blocks.body:
For treatment arm \(t\) and latent class \(u\), the latent conditional potential-outcome mean is
\[
\mu_{tu}:=E_P\!\left[Y(t)\mid U=u\right].
\]

blocks.title: Latent-class effect \(\tau_u\)
blocks.body:
For each latent class \(u\), its latent-class treatment effect is
\[
\tau_u:=\mu_{1u}-\mu_{0u}.
\]

blocks.title: Reference-proxy feature matrix \(A_t\)
blocks.body:
For treatment arm \(t\), the reference-proxy feature matrix \(A_t\in\mathbb R^{d_z\times k}\) is defined entrywise by
\[
A_t(i,u):=E_P\!\left[Z_i\mid U=u,T=t\right].
\]

blocks.title: Target-proxy feature matrix \(B\)
blocks.body:
The target-proxy feature matrix \(B\in\mathbb R^{d_x\times k}\) is defined entrywise by
\[
B(i,u):=E_P\!\left[X_i\mid U=u\right].
\]

blocks.title: Effect-support radius \(L_\tau\)
blocks.body:
The derived effect-support radius is
\[
L_\tau := \frac{4L\sqrt{d_z}}{\sigma_0}.
\]

blocks.title: Effect gap \(\delta(P)\)
blocks.body:
The effect gap of \(P\) is
\[
\delta(P)
:=
\min\bigl\{|\tau_u-\tau_v|:\ p_u>0,\ p_v>0,\ \tau_u\ne\tau_v\bigr\},
\]
with the convention \(\delta(P)=+\infty\) when the quotient law has a single distinct support point.

blocks.title: Observable population moments \(M_t(P)\), \(N_t(P)\), and \(m_X(P)\)
blocks.body:
For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), the observable armwise population moments and target-proxy population mean are
\[
M_t(P) := E_P[ZX^\top\mid T=t],
\qquad
N_t(P) := E_P[YZX^\top\mid T=t],
\qquad
m_X(P) := E_P[X].
\]

blocks.title: Atomic law coordinates
blocks.body:
For \(k\in\mathbb N\) and radius parameter \(L_\tau\in\mathbb R\), the represented atomic-law class
\[
\mathcal P_{\le k}([-L_\tau,L_\tau])
\]
is the labelled coordinate space whose element \(\xi\) consists of two real coordinate vectors,
\[
\xi=\bigl((w_i)_{i<k},(a_i)_{i<k}\bigr),
\qquad
w_i\in\mathbb R,\quad a_i\in\mathbb R .
\]
The abbreviation \(\mathcal P_k([-L_\tau,L_\tau])\) denotes the same represented space. The associated measure on \(\mathbb R\) is
\[
\nu_\xi=\sum_{i<k} \max\{w_i,0\}\,\delta_{a_i},
\]
so coincident labelled locations contribute additively at that location. The topology on this represented space is induced by the coordinate map
\[
\xi\mapsto \bigl((w_i)_{i<k},(a_i)_{i<k}\bigr),
\]
and its measurable structure is the pullback of the measurable structure on the two real coordinate vectors under the same map.

blocks.title: Ordered mass target \(p^{\uparrow}(P)\)
blocks.body:
When the \(k\) latent effects are distinct, \(p^{\uparrow}(P)\) is the vector of latent-class masses ordered by increasing effect. Otherwise,
\[
p^{\uparrow}(P) := (1/k,\ldots,1/k).
\]

blocks.title: Atom floor \(\operatorname{AtomFloor}(m,\xi)\)
blocks.body: For a probability law \(\xi\), \(\operatorname{AtomFloor}(m,\xi)\) is the condition that every distinct support atom of \(\xi\) has aggregate mass at least \(m\).

blocks.title: Reference-proxy separation
blocks.body:
Under the full-data law \(P\),
\[
Z\perp (X,Y)\mid (T,U).
\]

blocks.title: Target-proxy separation
blocks.body:
Under the full-data law \(P\),
\[
X\perp (Y,T)\mid U.
\]

blocks.title: Observed-outcome consistency
blocks.body:
Under the full-data law \(P\),
\[
Y=Y(T)
\]
almost surely.

blocks.title: Latent ignorability
blocks.body:
Under the full-data law \(P\), for each \(t\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
Y(t)\perp T\mid U.
\]

blocks.title: Target-proxy anchor
blocks.body:
Under the full-data law \(P\),
\[
X_1=1
\]
almost surely.

blocks.title: Bounded target proxy
blocks.body:
For the boundedness radius \(L\), under the full-data law \(P\),
\[
\lVert X\rVert_2\le L
\]
almost surely.

blocks.title: Bounded proxy product
blocks.body:
Under \(P\),
\[
\lVert ZX^\top\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le L
\]
almost surely.

blocks.title: Bounded outcome-proxy product
blocks.body:
Under \(P\),
\[
\lVert YZX^\top\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le L
\]
almost surely.

blocks.title: Latent-arm positivity
blocks.body:
The latent class and treatment arms satisfy
\[
\min_{1\le u\le k,\ t\in\{0,1\}} P(U=u,T=t)\ge \pi_0 .
\]

blocks.title: Proxy rank margin
blocks.body:
The reference- and target-proxy feature matrices satisfy
\[
\min\{\sigma_k(A_0),\sigma_k(A_1),\sigma_k(B)\}\ge \sigma_0 .
\]

blocks.title: Effect gap window
blocks.body:
The smallest positive effect gap satisfies
\[
g/2\le \delta(P)\le 2g .
\]

blocks.title: Distinct latent effects
blocks.body: The positive-mass latent effects \(\tau_u\) take exactly \(k\) distinct values.

blocks.title: Uniform proxy model class
blocks.body:
The uniformly conditioned proxy causal model class \(\mathcal M\) is the class of full-data probability laws \(P\) for records \((U,T,X,Z,Y(0),Y(1),Y)\) satisfying:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Record space.)} \(U\in\{1,\ldots,k\}\), \(T\in\{0,1\}\), \(X\in\mathbb R^{d_x}\), \(Z\in\mathbb R^{d_z}\), and \(Y(0),Y(1),Y\in\mathbb R\).
\item \textbf{(Parameter domain.)} The dimensions and constants obey
\[
2\le k,\qquad k\le d_x,\qquad k\le d_z,\qquad 1\le L,\qquad 0<\pi_0\le \frac{1}{2k},\qquad 0<\sigma_0\le 1.
\]
\item \textbf{(Model restrictions.)} \(P\) satisfies \cref{obj:ass:reference-proxy-separation,obj:ass:target-proxy-separation,obj:ass:consistency,obj:ass:latent-ignorability,obj:ass:anchor,obj:ass:bounded-x,obj:ass:bounded-proxy-product,obj:ass:bounded-outcome-proxy-product,obj:ass:latent-arm-positivity,obj:ass:proxy-rank-margin}.
\end{itemize}

blocks.title: Observable summary \(S(P)\) and metric \(d_S\)
blocks.body:
The observable conditional moment summary is
\[
S(P):=\bigl(M_0(P),M_1(P),N_0(P),N_1(P),m_X(P)\bigr).
\]
For summaries \(s\) and \(s'\), the summary metric is
\[
d_S(s,s')
:=
\sum_{j=1}^{4}\lVert s_j-s'_j\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
+\lVert s_5-s'_5\rVert_2.
\]

blocks.title: Empirical summary primitives \(\widehat S_n\)
blocks.body:
For an observed sample of size \(n\), let \(N_{t,n}\) be the number of observations in arm \(t\). Define the empirical armwise proxy moment \(\widehat M_{t,n}\) and outcome-proxy moment \(\widehat N_{t,n}\) using the total empty-arm convention:
\[
\widehat M_{t,n}
=
\frac{1}{\max\{1,N_{t,n}\}}
\sum_{i:T_i=t} Z_iX_i^\top,
\qquad
\widehat N_{t,n}
=
\frac{1}{\max\{1,N_{t,n}\}}
\sum_{i:T_i=t} Y_iZ_iX_i^\top .
\]
Let the empirical target-proxy mean be
\[
\widehat m_{X,n}
=
\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n X_i .
\]
The empirical five-block observable summary is
\[
\widehat S_n
=
\bigl(
\widehat M_{0,n},
\widehat M_{1,n},
\widehat N_{0,n},
\widehat N_{1,n},
\widehat m_{X,n}
\bigr).
\]

blocks.title: Empirical summary \(\widehat S_n\)
blocks.body:
For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), let
\[
N_{t,n}:=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mathbf 1\{T_i=t\}.
\]
Define
\[
\widehat M_{t,n}
:=
\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mathbf 1\{T_i=t\}Z_iX_i^\top}{\max\{1,N_{t,n}\}},
\qquad
\widehat N_{t,n}
:=
\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mathbf 1\{T_i=t\}Y_iZ_iX_i^\top}{\max\{1,N_{t,n}\}},
\]
and
\[
\widehat m_{X,n}:=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}X_i.
\]
The empirical five-block observable summary is
\[
\widehat S_n
:=
\bigl(\widehat M_{0,n},\widehat M_{1,n},
\widehat N_{0,n},\widehat N_{1,n},\widehat m_{X,n}\bigr).
\]
On the event \(\{N_{t,n}=0\}\), the corresponding armwise matrices \(\widehat M_{t,n}\) and \(\widehat N_{t,n}\) are the zero matrix, so \(\widehat S_n\) is a total Borel function of the sample.

blocks.title: First basis vector \(e_1\)
blocks.body: Let \(e_1\in\mathbb R^{d_x}\) be the first canonical basis vector.

blocks.title: Ambient Euclidean dimension
blocks.body: Let \(d\in\mathbb N\) denote the finite ambient dimension of a Euclidean summary space \(\mathbb R^d\). In the nearest-summary selection statement, \(\mathcal K\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) is a compact feasible set and \(d_S:\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) is the continuous summary distance used to choose nearest feasible summaries.

blocks.title: Vertical matrix stacking
blocks.body: For matrices \(A\in\mathbb R^{r\times d}\) and \(B\in\mathbb R^{s\times d}\) with the same number of columns, define \(\operatorname{stack}(A,B)\in\mathbb R^{(r+s)\times d}\) by vertical concatenation,\[\operatorname{stack}(A,B):=\begin{bmatrix}A\\ B\end{bmatrix}.\] Its row space is regarded as a subspace of \(\mathbb R^d\).

blocks.title: Compressed operator \(\Delta Q(P)\)
blocks.body:
Choose any matrix \(V(P)\in\mathbb R^{d_x\times k}\) with orthonormal columns spanning the row space of the vertically stacked matrix \(\operatorname{stack}(M_0(P),M_1(P))\subseteq\mathbb R^{d_x}\). Define
\[
\Delta Q(P)
:=
\{M_1(P)V(P)\}^{\dagger}N_1(P)V(P)
-
\{M_0(P)V(P)\}^{\dagger}N_0(P)V(P),
\]
with spectral anchors
\[
a(P)^\top:=m_X(P)^\top V(P),
\qquad
c(P):=V(P)^\top e_1.
\]

blocks.title: Quotient law \(\nu_P\)
blocks.body:
For \(P\in\mathcal M\) as in \cref{obj:def:model-class}, the quotient latent-effect law is
\[
\nu_P:=\sum_{u=1}^{k}p_u\delta_{\tau_u}.
\]
It is interpreted as a probability measure on the latent treatment effects, with coincident values of \(\tau_u\) carrying their aggregate mass.

blocks.title: Gap-local stratum
blocks.body: For a local effect-gap scale \(g\) satisfying \(0<g\le 1/4\), the gap-local stratum \(\mathcal M(g)\) is the class of full-data laws \(P\) in the uniformly conditioned proxy causal model class \(\mathcal M\) of \cref{obj:def:model-class} that satisfy \cref{obj:ass:gap-window,obj:ass:distinct-effects}.

blocks.title: Sample experiment \(\mathcal E_n\)
blocks.body:
The observed i.i.d. proxy experiment at sample size \(n\) is
\[
\mathcal E_n:=\{Q_P^{(n)}=P_O^{\otimes n}:P\in\mathcal M\}.
\]

blocks.title: Summary closure data
blocks.body:
For \(k,d_x,d_z\in\mathbb N\) and \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\), the summary-closure data consists of the closed feasible-summary set
\[
\mathcal K:=\overline{\mathscr S}^{\,d_S},
\qquad
\mathscr S:=S(\mathcal M)=\{S(P):P\in\mathcal M\},
\]
together with a quotient-law functional
\[
F:\mathscr S\to\mathcal P_k([-L_\tau,L_\tau]).
\]
For each admissible summary \(q\in\mathscr S\), \(F(q)\) is the quotient latent-effect law \(\nu_{P_q}\) of a selected model representative \(P_q\in\mathcal M\) satisfying \(S(P_q)=q\). The data also records the published spectral moment identity
\[
\int x^j\,d\nu_{P_q}(x)
=
a(P_q)^\top\Delta Q(P_q)^j c(P_q),
\qquad j=0,\ldots,2k-1,
\]
and, in the homogeneous-effect specialization with common effect \(\tau_\star\),
\[
\Delta Q(P_q)=\tau_\star I_k,
\qquad
\nu_{P_q}=\delta_{\tau_\star}.
\]

blocks.title: Observed VMW margins
blocks.body:
Fix \(k,d_x,d_z\in\mathbb N\) and \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\).  Suppose
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimensions.)} \(2\le k\), \(k\le d_x\), and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Margins.)} \(1\le L\), \(0<\pi_0\le 1/(2k)\), and \(0<\sigma_0\le 1\).
\item \textbf{(Uniform model class.)} The full-data law \(P\) belongs to the uniformly conditioned proxy causal model class \(\mathcal M\) in \cref{obj:def:model-class} with parameters \(k,d_x,d_z,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\).
\end{itemize}
Then the following quantitative observed-margin conclusions hold.  For each treatment arm \(t\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
P(T=t)\ge k\pi_0,
\]
and the observable armwise \(ZX^\top\) moment factors as
\[
M_t(P)
=
A_t\operatorname{diag}\{P(U=u\mid T=t):1\le u\le k\}B^\top .
\]
Moreover, for every orthonormal signal basis \(V\in\mathbb R^{d_x\times k}\) spanning the signal space of \(S(P)\),
\[
\sigma_k\{M_t(P)V\}
=
\sigma_k\{M_t(P)\},
\qquad
\pi_0\sigma_0^2\le \sigma_k\{M_t(P)V\}.
\]
The stacked observed proxy moment satisfies
\[
\pi_0\sigma_0^2
\le
\sigma_k\!\left(\operatorname{stack}(M_0(P),M_1(P))\right).
\]
The observable envelopes are
\[
\|M_t(P)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le L,
\qquad
\|N_t(P)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le L,
\qquad
\|m_X(P)\|_2\le L .
\]
Writing \(L_\tau=4L\sqrt{d_z}/\sigma_0\), for every latent class \(u\in\{1,\ldots,k\}\) and treatment arm \(t\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
|Y(t)|\le L_\tau/2
\quad\text{for \(P\)-almost every full-data record conditional on \(U=u\),}
\]
and
\[
|\mu_{tu}|\le L_\tau/2,
\qquad
|\tau_u|\le L_\tau .
\]
Finally, \(P\) belongs to the published VMW parameter class represented by the supplied scope handle.

cited_dependencies.statement: In the published VMW model, Assumption 1 includes \(Z\perp(X,Y)\mid(T,U)\), \(X\perp(Y,T)\mid U\), causal consistency \(Y=Y(T)\), and latent ignorability \(Y(t)\perp T\mid U\).  Assumption 2 requires \(A_0,A_1,B\) to have full column rank \(k\), and Section 4.2 uses strict latent positivity \(P(T=t\mid U=u)>0\).  These are qualitative conditions: the source does not impose the fixed margins \(\pi_0\) and \(\sigma_0\) used to define \(\mathcal M\).

blocks.title: Compact summary closure
blocks.body:
Let \(k,d_x,d_z\in\mathbb N\) and \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\). Let \(\mathcal M=\mathcal M(k,d_x,d_z,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)\) be the class of full-data probability laws satisfying the uniformly conditioned proxy causal model restrictions with boundedness radius \(L\), latent-arm positivity margin \(\pi_0\), and proxy-rank margin \(\sigma_0\). Define the admissible summary image and its closure by
\[
\mathscr S:=\{S(P):P\in\mathcal M\},
\qquad
\mathcal K:=\overline{\mathscr S}.
\]
For summaries \(s=(M_0,M_1,N_0,N_1,m_X)\) and \(q=(M_0',M_1',N_0',N_1',m_X')\), write
\[
d_S(s,q)
=
\|M_0-M_0'\|_{\mathrm{op}}
+\|M_1-M_1'\|_{\mathrm{op}}
+\|N_0-N_0'\|_{\mathrm{op}}
+\|N_1-N_1'\|_{\mathrm{op}}
+\Bigl(\sum_i (m_X(i)-m_X'(i))^2\Bigr)^{1/2}.
\]
Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Latent cardinality.)} \(2\le k\).
\item \textbf{(Proxy dimensions.)} \(k\le d_x\) and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Boundedness radius.)} \(1\le L\).
\item \textbf{(Latent-arm margin.)} \(0<\pi_0\le 1/(2k)\).
\item \textbf{(Proxy-rank margin.)} \(0<\sigma_0\le 1\).
\end{itemize}
Then there exists \(B\in\mathbb R\) such that
\[
d_S(s,0)\le B
\]
for every \(s\in\mathscr S\). Moreover, \(\mathcal K\) is compact, and
\[
\mathcal K\ne\varnothing
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\mathcal M\ne\varnothing .
\]

blocks.title: Simultaneous-concentration constant \(C_0\)
blocks.body:
Fix a simultaneous-concentration constant
\[
C_0\ge 1.
\]

blocks.title: Summary radius \(r_{n,\alpha}\)
blocks.body:
For \(n\ge 1\) and \(0<\alpha<1/2\), the simultaneous concentration radius is
\[
r_{n,\alpha}
:=
C_0L\sqrt{\frac{\log(C_0/\alpha)}{n}}.
\]

blocks.title: Ambient summary space
blocks.body:
For fixed proxy dimensions \(d_x\) and \(d_z\), the ambient five-block observable-summary space is
\[
\mathscr S_{\mathrm{all}}
:=
(\mathbb R^{d_z\times d_x})^4\times\mathbb R^{d_x}.
\]
A point \(s\in\mathscr S_{\mathrm{all}}\) is written \(s=(s_1,s_2,s_3,s_4,s_5)\), with four matrix blocks and one target-proxy mean block, and the summary metric is
\[
d_S(s,s'):=\sum_{j=1}^{4}\|s_j-s'_j\|_{\mathrm{op}}+\|s_5-s'_5\|_2 .
\]
The admissible image \(\mathscr S\) and its closure \(\mathcal K=\overline{\mathscr S}\) are subsets of \(\mathscr S_{\mathrm{all}}\), and the repair selector \(\Pi\) is a total Borel map from \(\mathscr S_{\mathrm{all}}\) to \(\mathscr S_{\mathrm{all}}\).

blocks.title: Summary-space repair map
blocks.body:
Fix \(k,d_x,d_z,n\in\mathbb N\) and \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\). Let
\[
L_\tau=\frac{4L\sqrt{d_z}}{\sigma_0},
\qquad
\mathcal K=\overline{\mathscr S},
\]
where \(\mathscr S\) is the admissible image in the five-block summary space. A summary-space repair datum consists of \(k>0\), \(L_\tau\ge 0\), and maps
\[
\overline F:\mathcal K\to \mathcal P_k([-L_\tau,L_\tau]),
\qquad
\Pi:\mathscr S_{\mathrm{all}}\to \mathscr S_{\mathrm{all}},
\]
with the following certified properties:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Extension.)} The map \(\overline F\) is continuous and, for every full-data law \(P\) in the uniformly conditioned model class, sends its observable summary \(S(P)\in\mathcal K\) to the quotient latent-effect law \(\nu_P\).
\item \textbf{(Nearest selector.)} The map \(\Pi\) is Borel measurable and, whenever \(\mathcal K\ne\varnothing\),
\[
\Pi(s)\in\mathcal K,
\qquad
d_S(\Pi(s),s)\le d_S(q,s)\quad\text{for every }q\in\mathcal K .
\]
\item \textbf{(Fallback.)} Whenever \(\mathcal K=\varnothing\), the selector satisfies
\[
\Pi(s)=0
\]
in the ambient five-block summary space for every \(s\).
\item \textbf{(Repair measurability.)} The sample-to-law map defined below is Borel measurable.
\end{itemize}
For an observed sample \(\omega:\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\to O_{d_x,d_z}\) with empirical five-block summary \(\widehat S_n(\omega)\), the repaired estimator is the total map
\[
\widehat\nu_n(\omega)=
\begin{cases}
\delta_0, & \mathcal K=\varnothing,\\
\overline F\bigl(\Pi(\widehat S_n(\omega))\bigr), & \mathcal K\ne\varnothing .
\end{cases}
\]

blocks.title: Structured-lattice constant \(C_{\mathrm{lat}}\)
blocks.body:
The structured-lattice constant is
\[
C_{\mathrm{lat}}
=
C_{\mathrm{lat}}(k,d_x,d_z,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0),
\]
the explicit prescribed constant given by the maximum of the threshold-stability constants and the grid-approximation constants displayed in the structured-lattice construction.

blocks.title: Structured lattice program
blocks.body:
For integers \(k,d_x,d_z,n\), constants \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\), and
\[
L_\tau:=4L\sqrt{d_z}/\sigma_0,
\]
a structured-lattice estimator \(A\) at radius \(L_\tau\) is prescribed when, writing \(N_A\) for the candidate count recorded in \(A\), there exist candidates
\[
\vartheta_i=(V_i,R_i,p_i,\tau_i),\qquad i\in\{1,\ldots,N_A\},
\]
and, for every sample \(\omega=(O_1,\ldots,O_n)\) of records in \(O_{d_x,d_z}\), a selected index
\[
i_\omega\in\{1,\ldots,N_A\},
\]
such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Well-formed exhaustive list.)} Each listed candidate \(\vartheta_i\) is well formed for the parameters \((n,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)\). Conversely, every well-formed structured lattice point \(\vartheta=(V,R,p,\tau)\) at radius \(L_\tau\) appears at some listed index \(i\) with
\[
V_i=V,\qquad R_i=R,\qquad p_i=p,\qquad \tau_i=\tau .
\]
\item \textbf{(No duplicates.)} If two listed candidates agree in all four displayed coordinates,
\[
V_i=V_j,\qquad R_i=R_j,\qquad p_i=p_j,\qquad \tau_i=\tau_j,
\]
then \(i=j\).
\item \textbf{(Lexicographic order.)} The index order agrees exactly with the lexicographic order on structured lattice points:
\[
i\le j
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\vartheta_i\le_{\mathrm{lex}}\vartheta_j .
\]
\item \textbf{(First minimizer.)} For the empirical summary \(s=\widehat S_n(\omega)\), the selected index minimizes the criterion \(J_n\) computed with threshold \(\pi_0\sigma_0^2/2\):
\[
J_n(\vartheta_{i_\omega};\widehat S_n(\omega))
\le
J_n(\vartheta_i;\widehat S_n(\omega))
\qquad\text{for every }i\in\{1,\ldots,N_A\}.
\]
Ties are resolved by the first lexicographic index:
\[
J_n(\vartheta_{i_\omega};\widehat S_n(\omega))
=
J_n(\vartheta_i;\widehat S_n(\omega))
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
i_\omega\le i .
\]
\item \textbf{(Returned law.)} On every sample \(\omega\), the estimator map recorded in \(A\) returns the atomic effect law attached to the selected candidate:
\[
\widehat\lambda_n(\omega)=\lambda_{\vartheta_{i_\omega}} .
\]
\end{itemize}

blocks.title: Uniform summary concentration
blocks.body:
Let \(k,d_x,d_z\in\mathbb N\), and let \(\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\). Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimensions.)} \(2\le k\), \(k\le d_x\), and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Positivity calibration.)} \(0<\pi_0\) and
\[
\pi_0\le \frac{1}{2k}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Rank-margin calibration.)} \(0<\sigma_0\) and \(\sigma_0\le 1\).
\end{itemize}
Then there exists a simultaneous-concentration constant \(C_0\in\mathbb R\) with \(1\le C_0\) such that the following holds. For every \(L\in\mathbb R\) and \(n\in\mathbb N\) with \(1\le L\) and \(1\le n\), every full-data probability law \(P\) on records \((U,T,X,Z,Y(0),Y(1),Y)\in \{1,\ldots,k\}\times\{0,1\}\times\mathbb R^{d_x}\times\mathbb R^{d_z}\times\mathbb R^3\) in the uniformly conditioned proxy causal model class \(\mathcal M\) with radius \(L\), latent-arm positivity margin \(\pi_0\), and proxy-rank singular-value margin \(\sigma_0\), and every tail probability \(\eta\) satisfying \(0<\eta<1/2\),
\[
Q_P^{(n)}\left\{d_S(\widehat S_n,S(P))>
C_0L\sqrt{\frac{\log(C_0/\eta)}{n}}\right\}\le \eta .
\]
Moreover, for each treatment arm \(t\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
Q_P^{(n)}\{N_{t,n}=0\}
=
\left(1-P_O\{O:T=t\}\right)^n
\le
(1-k\pi_0)^n .
\]

blocks.title: Gap-free modulus extension
blocks.body:
Fix natural numbers \(k,d_x,d_z\) and real constants \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\).  Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Latent dimension.)} \(2\le k\), \(k\le d_x\), and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Bound and margins.)} \(1\le L\), \(0<\pi_0\le (2k)^{-1}\), and \(0<\sigma_0\le 1\).
\end{itemize}
Let \(L_\tau=4L\sqrt{d_z}/\sigma_0\), and let \(\mathcal K=\overline{\mathscr S}\) be the summary closure from \cref{obj:def:summary-closure}.  For two summaries
\[
s=(M_0,M_1,N_0,N_1,m_X),
\qquad
q=(M'_0,M'_1,N'_0,N'_1,m'_X),
\]
write
\[
d_S(s,q)
=
\|M_0-M'_0\|+\|M_1-M'_1\|
+\|N_0-N'_0\|+\|N_1-N'_1\|
+\Bigl(\sum_i (m_X(i)-m'_X(i))^2\Bigr)^{1/2}.
\]
There exists a constant \(C_{\mathrm{mod}}>0\) such that, for every pair of full-data laws \(P,Q\in\mathcal M\),
\[
W_1(\nu_P,\nu_Q)\le C_{\mathrm{mod}}\,d_S(S(P),S(Q)).
\]
Moreover, there is a map
\[
\overline F:\mathcal K\to \mathcal P_k([-L_\tau,L_\tau])
\]
such that \(\overline F\) is continuous and Borel measurable,
\[
W_1(\overline F(q),\overline F(q'))
\le C_{\mathrm{mod}}\,d_S(q,q')
\qquad\text{for all }q,q'\in\mathcal K,
\]
and
\[
\overline F(S(Q))=\nu_Q
\qquad\text{for every }Q\in\mathcal M.
\]
This map is unique among continuous maps \(G:\mathcal K\to\mathcal P_k([-L_\tau,L_\tau])\) that obey
\[
W_1(G(q),G(q'))
\le C_{\mathrm{mod}}\,d_S(q,q')
\qquad\text{for all }q,q'\in\mathcal K
\]
and satisfy \(G(S(Q))=\nu_Q\) for every \(Q\in\mathcal M\): every such \(G\) satisfies \(G(q)=\overline F(q)\) for all \(q\in\mathcal K\).

blocks.title: Total Borel repair
blocks.body:
Let \(k,d_x,d_z,n\in\mathbb N\) and \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0,\alpha,C_0\in\mathbb R\).  Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimensions.)} \(2\le k\), \(k\le d_x\), and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Model radii.)} \(1\le L\), \(0<\pi_0\le 1/(2k)\), and \(0<\sigma_0\le 1\).
\item \textbf{(Sample size.)} \(1\le n\).
\item \textbf{(Confidence parameters.)} The miscoverage level satisfies \(0<\alpha<1/2\), and the simultaneous-concentration constant satisfies \(1\le C_0\).
\item \textbf{(Empirical summary.)} The empirical summary map \(\widehat S_n\) of \cref{obj:def:empirical-summary} is measurable.
\end{itemize}
Then there exists repair data \(R\) of the form specified in \cref{obj:def:summary-space-repair} such that the estimator \(\widehat\nu_n\) induced by \(R\) is Borel measurable.  Moreover, writing \(\mathcal K\) for the \(d_S\)-closure of the admissible summary image, if \(\mathcal K=\varnothing\), then for every sample \(\omega\),
\[
\widehat\nu_n(\omega)=\delta_0.
\]
For every sample \(\omega\), the sharp summary-inversion confidence set \(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}(\omega)\) associated with \(R\), with singleton value \(\{\delta_0\}\) when \(\mathcal K=\varnothing\) and otherwise consisting of the laws \(\nu=\overline F(q)\) with \(q\in\mathcal K\) and \(d_S(q,\Pi(\widehat S_n(\omega)))\le 2r_{n,\alpha}\), is nonempty.

blocks.title: Structured-lattice work count
blocks.body:
For the explicit structured-lattice estimator \(\widehat\lambda_n\), let \(\operatorname{Work}_n\) denote the fixed-dimensional exact-real operation count for forming \(\widehat S_n\), enumerating the lexicographically ordered candidate lattice, evaluating the criterion \(J_n\), and returning the first minimizer \(\widehat\vartheta_n\). In the fixed-dimensional unit-cost exact-real model, \(\operatorname{Work}_n\) counts arithmetic, comparison, singular-value, and fixed-degree root-isolation operations and satisfies
\[
\operatorname{Work}_n\le C\left\{n+n^{(d_xk+k^2+2k-1)/2}\right\},
\]
for a finite constant \(C=C(k,d_x,d_z,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)\).

blocks.title: Polynomial lattice estimator
blocks.body:
Fix integers \(k,d_x,d_z\) and constants \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\).  Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimension.)} \(2\le k\), \(k\le d_x\), and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Radius and margins.)} \(1\le L\), \(0<\pi_0\le (2k)^{-1}\), and \(0<\sigma_0\le 1\).
\end{itemize}
Put \(L_\tau:=4L\sqrt{d_z}/\sigma_0\) and \(s_0:=\pi_0\sigma_0^2\).  Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
c_V&:=4\sqrt{d_xk},
&
K_D&:=\frac{4\sqrt{k}LL_\tau}{\sigma_0},
&
A_D&:=\frac{8}{3s_0}+\frac{32L}{s_0^2},\\
K_f&:=\frac{16\sqrt{d_x}\,kL^2}{\sigma_0^2},
&
c_D&:=2K_Dc_V+\frac{4k\sqrt{k}LL_\tau}{\sigma_0^2}
+\frac{2\sqrt{k}L}{\sigma_0}+\frac{kL_\tau}{\sigma_0},\\
c_m&:=2\sqrt{k}Lc_V+k+kL,
&
c_b&:=k+2\sqrt{k}Lc_V,
&
c_{\mathrm{grid}}&:=c_D+c_m+c_b,\\
B_{\mathrm{lat}}&:=2(A_D+1)+c_{\mathrm{grid}},
&
C_{\mathrm{lat}}&:=\max\!\left\{\frac{8L_\tau}{s_0},
(L_\tau+K_D+LK_f)B_{\mathrm{lat}}\right\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Then \(C_{\mathrm{lat}}>0\), and there is a finite constant
\(C=C(k,d_x,d_z,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)>0\) such that, for every \(n\ge1\), there is a total Borel summary rule whose empirical-summary estimator \(\widehat\lambda_n\) is the lexicographically first minimizer over the prescribed structured lattice with effect radius \(L_\tau\), atom floor \(\pi_0\), and threshold \(s_0/2\).  For every sample, every distinct represented atom of \(\widehat\lambda_n\) has aggregate mass at least \(\pi_0\).

For every \(P\in\mathcal M\) in \cref{obj:def:model-class}, the stacked observable proxy moment at \(S(P)\), and at every summary \(s\) with
\[
d_S(s,S(P))<\frac{\pi_0\sigma_0^2}{2},
\]
has exactly its first \(k\) singular values at least \(\pi_0\sigma_0^2/2\) and all remaining singular values below \(\pi_0\sigma_0^2/2\).  The deterministic loss bound
\[
W_1(\widehat\lambda_n(\omega),\nu_P)
\le
C_{\mathrm{lat}}\left\{
d_S(\widehat S_n(\omega),S(P))+\frac{1}{\sqrt n}
\right\}
\]
holds for every sample \(\omega\), where \(\widehat S_n\) is the empirical summary in \cref{obj:def:empirical-summary}.  The candidate list and exhaustive-search operation count satisfy
\[
|\mathcal A_n|
\le C\, n^{(d_xk+k^2+2k-1)/2},
\qquad
\operatorname{Work}_n
\le
C\left(n+n^{(d_xk+k^2+2k-1)/2}\right).
\]
Finally, for every \(0<\eta<1/2\), every \(P\in\mathcal M\), and the observed product experiment \(Q_P^{(n)}\),
\[
Q_P^{(n)}\!\left\{
W_1(\widehat\lambda_n,\nu_P)>
C\sqrt{\frac{\log(C/\eta)}{n}}
\right\}
\le \eta .
\]

blocks.title: Collision-uniform root-n rate
blocks.body:
Fix integers \(k,d_x,d_z\) and constants \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\).  Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimensions.)} \(2\le k\), \(k\le d_x\), and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Uniform bounds.)} \(1\le L\), \(0<\pi_0\le 1/(2k)\), and \(0<\sigma_0\le 1\).
\end{itemize}
Then there is a constant \(C=C(k,d_x,d_z,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)>0\) such that, for every \(n\ge 1\), there exist a structured-lattice estimator \(\widehat\lambda_n\) taking values in \(\mathcal P_k([-L_\tau,L_\tau])\), with
\[
L_\tau=4L\sqrt{d_z}/\sigma_0,
\]
and a nearest-summary repair estimator \(\widehat\nu_n=\overline F(\Pi(\widehat S_n))\) from \cref{obj:def:summary-space-repair}, such that \(\widehat\lambda_n\) is the first lexicographic minimizer over a finite exhaustive structured lattice of well-formed candidates \(\vartheta\) for the criterion
\[
J_n(\vartheta;\widehat S_n),
\]
with tie-breaking by the lattice order and output \(\lambda_\vartheta\).  Both estimators are Borel sample maps.  For every \(\eta\) satisfying \(0<\eta<1/2\), every \(P\in\mathcal M\), and \(Q_P^{(n)}\)-sample,
\[
Q_P^{(n)}\!\left\{
\max\!\left\{
W_1(\widehat\lambda_n,\nu_P),
W_1(\widehat\nu_n,\nu_P)
\right\}
>
C\sqrt{\frac{\log(C/\eta)}{n}}
\right\}\le \eta .
\]
Moreover, for each treatment arm \(t\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
Q_P^{(n)}\{N_{t,n}=0\}\le (1-k\pi_0)^n .
\]

blocks.title: Wasserstein confidence set \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\)
blocks.body:
The inputs are fixed \(k,d_x,d_z,n\in\mathbb N\), constants \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0,\alpha,C_0,C_{\mathrm{lat}}\in\mathbb R\), an observed sample \(\omega\in O_{d_x,d_z}^n\) with empirical summary \(\widehat S_n\), repair data \((\overline F,\Pi)\) on \(\mathcal K\), and a prescribed structured-lattice estimator.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The fixed constants satisfy
\[
0<k,\qquad 0<n,\qquad 1\le L,\qquad
0<\pi_0\le (2k)^{-1},\qquad
0<\alpha<\frac12,\qquad
1\le C_0,\qquad 0<C_{\mathrm{lat}}.
\]
Define the effect-support radius and assume its nonnegativity:
\[
L_\tau:=\frac{4L\sqrt{d_z}}{\sigma_0},\qquad 0\le L_\tau.
\]
\item Define the simultaneous concentration radius by
\[
r_{n,\alpha}:=C_0L\sqrt{\frac{\log(C_0/\alpha)}{n}}.
\]
\item The repair data satisfy: \(\overline F\) is continuous on \(\mathcal K\) and extends the summary-to-quotient-law map on model summaries; \(\Pi\) is measurable; if \(\mathcal K\ne\varnothing\), then
\[
\Pi(s)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{q\in\mathcal K}d_S(q,s);
\]
if \(\mathcal K=\varnothing\), then
\[
\Pi(s)=0;
\]
and the induced repaired estimator is measurable.
\item Let \(\widehat\lambda_n\) be the valid \(k\)-atomic law returned at \(\omega\) by the measurable prescribed structured-lattice estimator at support radius \(L_\tau\), generated by an exhaustive duplicate-free lexicographically ordered list of well-formed \(H_n,q_n\) lattice candidates and the first lexicographic minimizer of \(J_n(\vartheta;\widehat S_n)\) with threshold
\[
\frac{\pi_0\sigma_0^2}{2}.
\]
\item Define the original summary-inversion confidence set by
\[
\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}:=
\begin{cases}
\{\overline F(q):q\in\mathcal K,\ d_S(q,\Pi(\widehat S_n))\le2r_{n,\alpha}\},&\mathcal K\ne\varnothing,\\
\{\delta_0\},&\mathcal K=\varnothing.
\end{cases}
\]
\item Define the atom-floor constant and computable radius by
\[
m_\star:=\pi_0,\qquad
R_{n,\alpha}:=C_{\mathrm{lat}}\left(r_{n,\alpha}+(\sqrt n)^{-1}\right).
\]
\item Define the atom-floor subclass by
\[
\mathcal P_{\le k,m_\star}([-L_\tau,L_\tau])
:=
\{\xi\in\mathcal P_{\le k}([-L_\tau,L_\tau]):
\operatorname{AtomFloor}(m_\star,\xi)\}.
\]
\item Output the computable Wasserstein confidence set
\[
\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}
:=
\{\xi\in\mathcal P_{\le k}([-L_\tau,L_\tau]):
\operatorname{AtomFloor}(m_\star,\xi),\
W_1(\xi,\widehat\lambda_n)\le R_{n,\alpha}\}.
\]
\end{enumerate}

blocks.title: Cluster report \(\mathfrak R_{n,\alpha}\)
blocks.body:
The cluster report is computed from \(\widehat S_n\), \(S(P)\), \(r_{n,\alpha}\), \(R_{n,\alpha}\), \(m_\star\), \(\widehat\lambda_n\), and \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\) as follows.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Define the simultaneous concentration event and association radius by
\[
E_P:=\{d_S(\widehat S_n,S(P))\le r_{n,\alpha}\},
\qquad
\rho_{n,\alpha}:=\frac{R_{n,\alpha}}{m_\star}.
\]
\item Merge repeated atoms of \(\widehat\lambda_n\). Join two distinct support points whenever their distance is at most \(4\rho_{n,\alpha}\), and define
\[
\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}
\]
as the set of connected components of the resulting graph.
\item For each \(C\in\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\), define the associated true and candidate support sets by
\[
K_C(P):=\{x\in\operatorname{supp}(\nu_P):\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\le\rho_{n,\alpha}\},
\qquad
K_C(\xi):=\{x\in\operatorname{supp}(\xi):\operatorname{dist}(x,C)\le\rho_{n,\alpha}\}.
\]
\item Define the mass interval by
\[
I_C:=\left[
\inf_{\xi\in\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}}\xi(K_C(\xi)),
\sup_{\xi\in\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}}\xi(K_C(\xi))
\right].
\]
In the ordered-support and transport-plan representation of \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\), each endpoint is the value of a finite union of fixed-dimensional mixed-integer constrained programs. For each \(1\le r\le k\), introduce binary variables
\[
z_a\in\{0,1\},\qquad 1\le a\le r,
\]
with
\[
z_a=1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \min_{c\in C}|x_a-c|\le\rho_{n,\alpha},
\]
and minimize or maximize
\[
\sum_{a=1}^r w_a z_a
\]
subject to the ordered-support, atom-floor, simplex, and transport constraints defining \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\).
\item Output the report
\[
\mathfrak R_{n,\alpha}
:=
\left\{
\left(
C,\,
[\min C-\rho_{n,\alpha},\max C+\rho_{n,\alpha}],\,
I_C
\right):
C\in\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}
\right\}.
\]
For each component \(C\), define the external true-support gap by
\[
\Delta_C(P):=\inf\{|x-y|:x\in K_C(P),\ y\in\operatorname{supp}(\nu_P)\setminus K_C(P)\},
\]
with value \(+\infty\) when \(\operatorname{supp}(\nu_P)\setminus K_C(P)=\emptyset\).
\end{enumerate}

blocks.title: Ordered-weight estimator \(\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}\)
blocks.body:
The input is the positive estimated atomic law \(\widehat\nu_n\) on \([-L_\tau,L_\tau]\).

\begin{enumerate}
\item Write \(\widehat\nu_n\) uniquely in increasing support order as
\[
\widehat\nu_n
=
\sum_{\ell=1}^{\widehat s_n}
\widehat w_{\ell,n}\delta_{\widehat\tau_{\ell,n}},
\qquad
\widehat\tau_{1,n}<\cdots<\widehat\tau_{\widehat s_n,n},
\qquad
\widehat w_{\ell,n}>0 .
\]

\item Output the ordered-weight estimator
\[
\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}
=
\begin{cases}
(\widehat w_{1,n},\ldots,\widehat w_{k,n}), & \widehat s_n=k,\\[2mm]
(1/k,\ldots,1/k), & \widehat s_n<k .
\end{cases}
\]
\end{enumerate}

Ordering the finitely many support points and extracting their jump sizes are Borel operations, so \(\widehat\nu_n\mapsto\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}\) is a total Borel map into \(\Delta^{k-1}\).

blocks.title: Honest root-\(n\) confidence
blocks.body:
Fix integers \(k,d_x,d_z\) and constants \(\pi_0,\sigma_0\) such that
\[
2\le k,\qquad k\le d_x,\qquad k\le d_z,\qquad
0<\pi_0\le {1\over 2k},\qquad 0<\sigma_0\le 1 .
\]
There exists a simultaneous-concentration constant \(C_0\ge 1\) such that, for every boundedness radius \(L\ge 1\), there is a constant \(C_{\mathrm{mod}}>0\) for which the prescribed structured-lattice constant \(C_{\mathrm{lat}}\) is positive and the following holds.  For every sample size \(n\ge 1\), there exist:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Structured lattice estimator.)} a measurable estimator \(\widehat\lambda_n\) taking values in \(\mathcal P_k([-L_\tau,L_\tau])\), generated by a finite exhaustive list of well-formed structured-lattice candidates, ordered lexicographically, with \(\widehat\lambda_n\) equal to the effect law of the first lexicographic minimizer of the structured-lattice criterion;
\item \textbf{(Summary repair data.)} a continuous extension \(\overline F\) on the summary closure \(\mathcal K\), a measurable nearest-summary selector \(\Pi\) with its empty-closure fallback, and the associated measurable repaired summary-to-law map.
\end{itemize}
For every miscoverage level \(\alpha\) satisfying
\[
0<\alpha< {1\over 2},
\]
let \(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\), \(R_{n,\alpha}\), and \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\) be the confidence-set objects of \cref{obj:def:wasserstein-confidence-set} formed from this repair data and this structured-lattice estimator, with \(m_\star=\pi_0\) and center \(\widehat\lambda_n\).  Then, on every sample, both \(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\) and \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\) are nonempty, and \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\) has the finite constrained transport representation
\[
\nu\in\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\operatorname{AtomFloor}(\pi_0,\nu)\ \text{and there exists a transport plan }\gamma\text{ from }\nu\text{ to }\widehat\lambda_n
\text{ with cost at most }R_{n,\alpha}.
\]
Moreover, for every full-data probability law \(P\in\mathcal M\) in \cref{obj:def:model-class},
\[
1-\alpha
\le
Q_P^{(n)}
\left\{
\nu_P\in\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\cap\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}
\right\}.
\]
Finally, on every sample,
\[
\operatorname{diam}_{W_1}(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha})
\le
4C_{\mathrm{mod}}\, r_{n,\alpha},
\qquad
\operatorname{diam}_{W_1}(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha})
\le
2R_{n,\alpha}.
\]

blocks.title: Cluster-adaptive report validity
blocks.body:
Let \(k,d_x,d_z\in\mathbb N\), \(\pi_0\in\mathbb R\), and \(\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\).  Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimensions.)} \(2\le k\), \(k\le d_x\), and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Latent mass.)} \(0<\pi_0\le 1/(2k)\).
\item \textbf{(Rank margin.)} \(0<\sigma_0\le 1\).
\end{itemize}
Then there is a simultaneous-concentration constant \(C_0\ge 1\) such that, for every \(L\ge 1\), if
\[
L_\tau=\frac{4L\sqrt{d_z}}{\sigma_0},
\]
and
\[
\begin{gathered}
s_0=\pi_0\sigma_0^2,\qquad
c_V=4\sqrt{d_xk},\qquad
K_D=\frac{4\sqrt{k}LL_\tau}{\sigma_0},\\
A_D=\frac{8}{3s_0}+\frac{32L}{s_0^2},\qquad
K_f=\frac{16\sqrt{d_x}kL^2}{\sigma_0^2},\\
c_D=2K_Dc_V+\frac{4k\sqrt{k}LL_\tau}{\sigma_0^2}
      +\frac{2\sqrt{k}L}{\sigma_0}+\frac{kL_\tau}{\sigma_0},\\
c_m=2\sqrt{k}Lc_V+k+kL,\qquad
c_b=k+2\sqrt{k}Lc_V,\\
c_{\mathrm{grid}}=c_D+c_m+c_b,\qquad
B_{\mathrm{lat}}=2(A_D+1)+c_{\mathrm{grid}},
\end{gathered}
\]
then the prescribed structured-lattice stability constant
\[
C_{\mathrm{lat}}
=
\max\left\{
\frac{8L_\tau}{s_0},
\,
(L_\tau+K_D+LK_f)B_{\mathrm{lat}}
\right\}
\]
is positive.  For every \(n\ge 1\), there exist a measurable structured-lattice estimator
\(\widehat\lambda_n\) and repair data consisting of a continuous extension on \(\mathcal K\) and a Borel nearest-summary selector, such that \(\widehat\lambda_n\) is obtained from an exhaustive lexicographically ordered finite list of well-formed structured-lattice candidates by choosing the first minimizer of \(J_n(\vartheta;\widehat S_n)\).

For every \(\alpha\) with \(0<\alpha<1/2\), the estimator has atom floor \(\pi_0\).  Moreover, for every \(P\in\mathcal M\) in \cref{obj:def:model-class} and every sample,
\[
W_1\!\left(\widehat\lambda_n,\nu_P\right)
\le
C_{\mathrm{lat}}
\left\{
d_S\!\left(\widehat S_n,S(P)\right)+\frac{1}{\sqrt n}
\right\}.
\]
Define
\[
r_{n,\alpha}
=
C_0L\sqrt{\frac{\log(C_0/\alpha)}{n}},
\qquad
R_{n,\alpha}
=
C_{\mathrm{lat}}\left(r_{n,\alpha}+\frac{1}{\sqrt n}\right),
\qquad
\rho_{n,\alpha}=\frac{R_{n,\alpha}}{\pi_0},
\]
with \(\widehat S_n\) as in \cref{obj:def:empirical-summary}, and set
\[
E_P=\left\{\omega:
d_S\!\left(\widehat S_n(\omega),S(P)\right)\le r_{n,\alpha}
\right\}.
\]
Then
\[
Q_P^{(n)}(E_P)\ge 1-\alpha.
\]
For every sample \(\omega\in E_P\), the cluster report \(\mathfrak R_{n,\alpha}\) centered at \(\widehat\lambda_n(\omega)\) satisfies the following properties for the representative atomic law \(\nu_P\):
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Partition.)} Each support point \(x\in\operatorname{supp}(\nu_P)\) belongs to a unique empirical component \(C\in\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\) with \(x\in K_C(P)\).
\item \textbf{(Association.)} For every \(C\in\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\), the set \(K_C(P)\) is nonempty and is contained in \(\operatorname{supp}(\nu_P)\).
\item \textbf{(Support interval.)} If \(C\in\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\) and \(x\in K_C(P)\), then \(x\) lies in the reported support interval for \(C\).
\item \textbf{(Mass interval.)} If \(C\in\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\), then the reported mass interval \(I_C\) contains \(\nu_P(K_C(P))\).
\item \textbf{(Singleton width.)} If \(C\in\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\) and \(\operatorname{card}(K_C(P))=1\), then the reported support interval for \(C\) has length at most \(4\rho_{n,\alpha}\), and
\[
\operatorname{length}(I_C)
\le
\frac{8}{\pi_0}
\min\left\{1,\frac{R_{n,\alpha}}{\delta(P)}\right\}.
\]
\item \textbf{(External-gap width.)} If \(C\in\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\) and \(\Delta_C(P)=+\infty\), then \(\operatorname{length}(I_C)=0\).  For every \(C\in\widehat{\mathscr K}_{n,\alpha}\),
\[
\operatorname{length}(I_C)
\le
\frac{8}{\pi_0}
\min\left\{1,\frac{R_{n,\alpha}}{\Delta_C(P)}\right\},
\]
with the displayed right side read as zero when \(\Delta_C(P)=+\infty\).
\item \textbf{(Constrained representation.)} The computable class
\(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\) has the finite constrained-program representation
\[
\xi\in\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\operatorname{AtomFloor}(\pi_0,\xi)
\ \text{and}\ 
\exists\gamma\ \text{with transport cost at most } R_{n,\alpha}
\text{ from }\xi\text{ to }\widehat\lambda_n(\omega).
\]
\end{itemize}

blocks.title: Ordered-weight upper bound
blocks.body:
Let \(k,d_x,d_z\in\mathbb N\) and \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\).  Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Latent size.)} \(2\le k\).
\item \textbf{(Proxy dimensions.)} \(k\le d_x\) and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Envelope.)} \(1\le L\).
\item \textbf{(Latent-arm margin.)} \(0<\pi_0\le (2k)^{-1}\).
\item \textbf{(Rank margin.)} \(0<\sigma_0\le 1\).
\end{itemize}
Then there is a constant \(C=C(k,d_x,d_z,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)>0\) such that, for every \(n\ge1\), one can choose the simplex-valued measurable ordered-weight estimator \(\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}\) from \cref{obj:def:labeled-weight-estimator} so that, for every gap scale \(g\) satisfying \(0<g\le1/4\) and every full-data probability law \(P\in\mathcal M(g)\),
\[
E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\!\left[\left\|\widehat p_n^{\uparrow}-p^{\uparrow}(P)\right\|_1\right]
\le
C\min\left\{1,\left(\sqrt n\,g\right)^{-1}\right\}.
\]

blocks.title: Local Kullback--Leibler radius \(c_{\mathrm{loc}}\)
blocks.body:
Fix a local Kullback--Leibler radius constant \(c_{\mathrm{loc}}\) satisfying
\[
0<c_{\mathrm{loc}}<1.
\]

blocks.title: Factorization-preserving two-class path law $P_{g,h}$
blocks.body: For $0\le g\le 1/4$ and $|h|\le 1/100$, $P_{g,h}$ is the full-data law on $(U,T,X,Z,Y(0),Y(1),Y)$ with $U\in\{1,2\}$, $T\in\{0,1\}$, $X=(1,X_2)^\top$, $Z=(1,Z_2)^\top$, $Y=Y(T)$, latent masses $P_{g,h}(U=1)=2/5+h$ and $P_{g,h}(U=2)=3/5-h$, and latent-arm weights\[\begin{array}{c|cc} & u=1 & u=2\\ \hline P_{g,h}(U=u,T=1) & 4/25+3h/5 & 9/25-3h/5\\ P_{g,h}(U=u,T=0) & 6/25+2h/5 & 6/25-2h/5 .\end{array}\] Thus $P_{g,h}(T=1\mid U=u)=P_{g,h}(U=u,T=1)/P_{g,h}(U=u)$. Conditional on $U$, the variables $T,X_2,Y(0),Y(1)$ are Bernoulli with the displayed treatment probability, with $E_{P_{g,h}}[X_2\mid U=1]=1/5$, $E_{P_{g,h}}[X_2\mid U=2]=(12/25-h/5)/(3/5-h)$, $E_{P_{g,h}}[Y(0)\mid U=u]=1/4$, $E_{P_{g,h}}[Y(1)\mid U=1]=1/2-g/2$, and $E_{P_{g,h}}[Y(1)\mid U=2]=1/2+g/2$. Conditional on $(U,T)$, $Z_2$ is Bernoulli and independent of $(X_2,Y(0),Y(1))$, with\[E_{P_{g,h}}[Z_2\mid U=1,T=1]=\frac{225h+28}{20(15h+4)},\quad E_{P_{g,h}}[Z_2\mid U=2,T=1]=\frac34,\]\[E_{P_{g,h}}[Z_2\mid U=1,T=0]=\frac{35h+9}{10(5h+3)},\quad E_{P_{g,h}}[Z_2\mid U=2,T=0]=\frac7{10}.\] With the induced feature matrices $A_t(h)$ and $B(h)$ and latent-arm weight vector $w_t(h)=(P_{g,h}(U=1,T=t),P_{g,h}(U=2,T=t))$, the path preserves the armwise proxy factorization $A_t(h)\operatorname{diag}(w_t(h))B(h)^\top=A_t(0)\operatorname{diag}(w_t(0))B(0)^\top$ for $t\in\{0,1\}$, and $P_{g,0}=P^{\mathrm{wit}}_{g/2}$.

blocks.title: Path law \(P_{g,h}\)
blocks.body: For a gap \(g\) and displacement \(h\), \(P_{g,h}\) is the explicit two-class factorization-preserving path law obtained by perturbing the latent weights while preserving the stated proxy factorizations.

blocks.title: Published VMW scope handle
blocks.body:
The published VMW scope handle is the cited-publication interface for the proxy-model parameter class and recovery regime. For fixed latent cardinality \(k\), target-proxy dimension \(d_x\), reference-proxy dimension \(d_z\), and full-data law \(P\) on \((U,T,X,Z,Y(0),Y(1),Y)\), it records three law-level predicates:
\[
\mathsf{Model}_{\mathrm{VMW}}(k,d_x,d_z,P),
\qquad
\mathsf{FiniteReg}_{\mathrm{VMW}}(k,d_x,d_z,P),
\qquad
\mathsf{Recover}_{\mathrm{VMW}}(k,d_x,d_z,P).
\]
These predicates are publication-level gates whose concrete interpretations enter through separate cited gates. The handle also includes the published estimator
\[
\widehat\Theta^{\mathrm{VMW}}_n:
(O_{d_x,d_z})^n
\to
\mathbb R^k\times\mathbb R^{d_x\times k}\times\mathbb R^k,
\]
which maps an observed sample of size \(n\) from records \((T,X,Z,Y)\) to a triple consisting of treatment effects, an anchor-normalized target-proxy feature matrix, and real-valued weight coordinates.

blocks.title: Kullback--Leibler divergence $D_{\mathrm{KL}}$
blocks.body:
For probability laws $\mu$ and $
u$ on the same measurable space, define $D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\mu\|
u):=\int \log(d\mu/d
u)\,d\mu$ when $\mu\ll
u$, and set $D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\mu\|
u):=+\infty$ when $\mu
ot\ll
u$. In the local experiments this divergence is applied to one-record observed-data margins such as $P_O$ and $(P_0^{\mathrm{wit}})_O$.

blocks.title: Kullback--Leibler divergence
blocks.body:
For probability laws $\mu$ and $
u$ on the same measurable space, the Kullback--Leibler divergence from $
u$ to $\mu$ is
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\mu\|
u):=\int \log\!\left( rac{d\mu}{d
u}ight)\,d\mu
\]
when $\mu\ll
u$, and $D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\mu\|
u):=+\infty$ when $\mu
ot\ll
u$. In the local experiments this divergence is applied to one-record observed-data margins, including $P_O$ and $(P_0^{\mathrm{wit}})_O$.

blocks.title: Local quotient neighborhood
blocks.body:
The Kullback--Leibler divergence from \(P_O\), the observed-data marginal, to the observed margin of \(P_0^{\mathrm{wit}}\), the two-class collision witness at perturbation zero, satisfies
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\bigl(P_O\Vert (P_0^{\mathrm{wit}})_O\bigr)\le \frac{c_{\mathrm{loc}}}{n}.
\]

blocks.title: Local weight neighborhood
blocks.body:
The Kullback--Leibler divergence from \(P_O\), the observed-data marginal, to the observed margin of the two-class witness at perturbation \(g/2\) satisfies
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\bigl(P_O\Vert (P_{g/2}^{\mathrm{wit}})_O\bigr)\le \frac{c_{\mathrm{loc}}}{n}.
\]

blocks.title: Two-class witness law \(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}\)
blocks.body:
For \(k=d_x=d_z=2\), the two-class witness law \(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}\) is the law specified by
\[
P(U=1)=0.4,\qquad P(U=2)=0.6,
\]
\[
P(T=1\mid U=1)=0.4,\qquad P(T=1\mid U=2)=0.6,
\]
\[
X=(1,X_2)^\top,\qquad Z=(1,Z_2)^\top,
\]
\[
B=\begin{psmallmatrix}1&1\\0.2&0.8\end{psmallmatrix},
\qquad
A_0=\begin{psmallmatrix}1&1\\0.3&0.7\end{psmallmatrix},
\qquad
A_1=\begin{psmallmatrix}1&1\\0.35&0.75\end{psmallmatrix},
\]
\[
E[Y(0)\mid U]=(0.25,0.25),
\qquad
E[Y(1)\mid U]=(0.5-\varepsilon,0.5+\varepsilon).
\]
Conditional on \(U\), the variables \(X_2\), \(Y(0)\), \(Y(1)\), and \(T\) are mutually independent Bernoulli variables with the displayed conditional means. Conditional on \(U\) and \(T\), the variable \(Z_2\) is independent of \((X_2,Y(0),Y(1))\) and has conditional mean given by \(A_T\). The observed outcome is
\[
Y=Y(T).
\]

blocks.title: Local quotient experiment \(\mathcal L_n^\nu\)
blocks.body:
The local quotient-law KL experiment is
\[
\mathcal L_n^\nu
:=
\{P\in\mathcal M:P\text{ satisfies }\cref{obj:ass:local-quotient-neighborhood}\},
\]
where \(\mathcal M\) is the model class in \cref{obj:def:model-class}.

blocks.title: Local weight experiment \(\mathcal L_{n,g}^p\)
blocks.body:
The local labeled-weight KL experiment is
\[
\mathcal L_{n,g}^p
:=
\{P\in\mathcal M(g):P\text{ satisfies }\cref{obj:ass:local-weight-neighborhood}\},
\]
where \(\mathcal M(g)\) is the gap-local stratum in \cref{obj:def:gap-stratum}.

blocks.title: Two-class witness validity
blocks.body:
For every collision-witness effect displacement \(\varepsilon\) satisfying
\[
0\le \varepsilon \le \frac18,
\]
the explicit two-class Bernoulli proxy witness law \(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}\) belongs to \(\mathcal M\) with \(L=2\), \(\pi_0=0.1\), and \(\sigma_0=0.1\). Moreover,
\[
P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}(T=0)=0.48,\qquad
P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}(T=1)=0.52,
\]
\[
\det(B)=0.6,\qquad
\det(A_0)=\det(A_1)=0.4,
\]
\[
\det(M_0(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}))=0.06,\qquad
\det(M_1(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}))=0.4\cdot 0.6\cdot \frac{36}{169},
\]
and the quotient latent-effect law is
\[
\nu_{P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}}
=
0.4\,\delta_{0.25-\varepsilon}
+
0.6\,\delta_{0.25+\varepsilon}.
\]
At \(\varepsilon=0\), the proxy feature and observable moment matrices above are nonsingular, the quotient latent-effect law is \(\delta_{0.25}\), and the two latent-class masses are distinct.

blocks.title: Matching local lower bounds
blocks.body:
Fix \(c_{\mathrm{loc}}\in(0,1)\). There exist constants \(a,c,C\in\mathbb R\) such that
\[
0<a\le \frac18,\qquad c>0,\qquad C>0,
\]
and, for every integer \(n\ge 1\), the following statements hold for the explicit submodel \(k=d_x=d_z=2\), \(L=2\), \(\pi_0=1/10\), and \(\sigma_0=1/10\).
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Quotient-law risk.)} For every measurable quotient-law estimator \(\widetilde\nu_n\) with support radius
\[
L_\tau=\frac{4L\sqrt{d_z}}{\sigma_0},
\]
there is a law \(P\) in the local quotient-law experiment \(\mathcal L_n^\nu\) of \cref{obj:def:local-quotient-experiment} such that
\[
P=P_0^{\mathrm{wit}}
\quad\text{or}\quad
P=P_{a/\sqrt n}^{\mathrm{wit}},
\]
with \(P_\varepsilon^{\mathrm{wit}}\) as in \cref{obj:def:two-class-witness}, and
\[
\frac{c}{\sqrt n}
\le
E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\!\left[W_1(\widetilde\nu_n,\nu_P)\right].
\]

\item \textbf{(Ordered-weight risk.)} For every \(g\in(0,1/4]\) and every measurable ordered-weight estimator \(\widetilde p_n\) taking values in the simplex, there is a law \(P\) in the local labeled-weight experiment \(\mathcal L_{n,g}^{p}\) of \cref{obj:def:local-weight-experiment} such that
\[
P=P_{g,0}
\quad\text{or}\quad
P=P_{g,h(n,g)},
\qquad
h(n,g)=a\min\left\{1,\frac{1}{\sqrt n\,g}\right\},
\]
and
\[
c\min\left\{1,\frac{1}{\sqrt n\,g}\right\}
\le
E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\!\left[\|\widetilde p_n-p^{\uparrow}(P)\|_1\right].
\]

\item \textbf{(Quotient-law certificate.)} The laws \(P_0^{\mathrm{wit}}\) and \(P_{a/\sqrt n}^{\mathrm{wit}}\) belong to the corresponding local quotient-law experiments, and their observed-data marginals and quotient laws satisfy
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left((P_{a/\sqrt n}^{\mathrm{wit}})_O\Vert (P_0^{\mathrm{wit}})_O\right)
\le
\frac{C}{n},
\qquad
\frac{c}{\sqrt n}
\le
W_1\!\left(\nu_{P_0^{\mathrm{wit}}},\nu_{P_{a/\sqrt n}^{\mathrm{wit}}}\right).
\]

\item \textbf{(Labeled-path certificate.)} For every \(g\in(0,1/4]\), with
\[
h=h(n,g)=a\min\left\{1,\frac{1}{\sqrt n\,g}\right\},
\]
the displacement \(h\) lies in the tangent-amplitude domain, the laws \(P_{g,h}\) and \(P_{g,0}\) belong to the corresponding local labeled-weight experiments, and
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left((P_{g,h})_O\Vert (P_{g,0})_O\right)
\le
C g^2h^2,
\qquad
\sum_i\left|p_i^{\uparrow}(P_{g,h})-p_i^{\uparrow}(P_{g,0})\right|
=
2|h|.
\]
\end{itemize}

blocks.title: Same-class quotient minimax
blocks.body:
For the specialization \(k=d_x=d_z=2\), \(L=2\), \(\pi_0=1/10\), and \(\sigma_0=1/10\), let \(\mathcal M\) be the uniformly conditioned proxy causal model class in \cref{obj:def:model-class}.  The derived effect-support radius is
\[
L_\tau=4L\sqrt{d_z}/\sigma_0=80\sqrt 2 .
\]
There exist real constants \(c\) and \(C\) such that
\[
0<c<C
\]
and, for every sample size \(n\ge 1\), the following two statements hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Lower bound.)} For every measurable estimator \(\widetilde\nu_n\) mapping an \(n\)-sample of observed records to a represented atomic law modulo the radius \(L_\tau\), there exists a full-data probability law \(P\in\mathcal M\) such that
\[
\frac{c}{\sqrt n}
\le
E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\!\left[
  W_1\!\left(\widetilde\nu_n,\nu_P\right)
\right].
\]
\item \textbf{(Upper bound.)} There exists a measurable estimator \(\widetilde\nu_n\) mapping an \(n\)-sample of observed records to a represented atomic law modulo the radius \(L_\tau\) such that, for every full-data probability law \(P\in\mathcal M\),
\[
E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\!\left[
  W_1\!\left(\widetilde\nu_n,\nu_P\right)
\right]
\le
\frac{C}{\sqrt n}.
\]
\end{itemize}
Equivalently, on this same specialized class,
\[
\frac{c}{\sqrt n}
\le
\inf_{\widetilde\nu_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}
E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\!\left[
  W_1\!\left(\widetilde\nu_n,\nu_P\right)
\right]
\le
\frac{C}{\sqrt n}
\]
for every \(n\ge 1\), where the infimum ranges over measurable estimators with output radius \(L_\tau\).

blocks.title: Same-class labeled minimax
blocks.body:
There exist real constants \(c\) and \(C\) such that \(0<c<C\) and, for every sample size \(n\ge 1\) and every gap scale \(g\) with \(0<g\le 1/4\), the gap stratum \(\mathcal M(g)\) from \cref{obj:def:gap-stratum} satisfies
\[
c\min\left\{1,\frac{1}{\sqrt n\,g}\right\}
\le
\inf_{\widetilde p_n}
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M(g)}
E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\!\left[
\left\|\widetilde p_n-p^{\uparrow}(P)\right\|_1
\right]
\le
C\min\left\{1,\frac{1}{\sqrt n\,g}\right\}.
\]
Here the infimum is over all measurable simplex-valued labeled weight estimators based on \(n\) observed records in the explicit submodel \(k=d_x=d_z=2\), \(L=2\), \(\pi_0=1/10\), and \(\sigma_0=1/10\), and \(p^{\uparrow}(P)\) is the effect-ordered latent-mass vector with the barycentric collision fallback.

blocks.title: Calibrated path displacement
blocks.body:
For \(a,g\in\mathbb R\) and \(n\in\mathbb N\), define
\[
\operatorname{calibratedDisplacement}(a,n,g)
=
a\,\min\{1,(\sqrt n\,g)^{-1}\}.
\]

blocks.title: Published VMW finite-regularity condition
blocks.body: A law \(P\) satisfies the published VMW finite-regularity condition when \(0<k\), \(k\le d_x\), \(k\le d_z\), and there exist constants \(L_X,L_{ZX},L_{YZX},\pi,\sigma>0\) such that \(\lVert X\rVert_2\le L_X\), \(\lVert ZX^\top\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le L_{ZX}\), and \(\lVert YZX^\top\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le L_{YZX}\) almost surely, \(P(T=t)\ge\pi\) for \(t\in\{0,1\}\), and there is a top-\(k\) right singular basis \(V\) for the stacked proxy moment \([M_0(P);M_1(P)]\) satisfying \(\sigma_k([M_0(P);M_1(P)])\ge\sigma\) and \(\sigma_k(M_t(P)V)\ge\sigma\) for each \(t\in\{0,1\}\).

blocks.title: Published VMW structural model
blocks.body: Fix \(k,d_x,d_z\) with \(0<k\), \(k\le d_x\), and \(k\le d_z\). A one-unit full-data probability law \(P\) belongs to the published VMW structural model when it satisfies the published qualitative proxy model conditions: reference-proxy separation \(Z\perp (X,Y)\mid(T,U)\), target-proxy separation \(X\perp (Y,T)\mid U\), consistency \(Y=Y(T)\) almost surely, armwise latent ignorability \(Y(t)\perp T\mid U\) for \(t\in\{0,1\}\), full column rank of \(A_0\), \(A_1\), and \(B\), and strict latent-arm positivity \(P(U=u,T=t)>0\) for every \(u\in\{1,\ldots,k\}\) and \(t\in\{0,1\}\).

blocks.title: Separated recovery regime
blocks.body:
A full-data law \(P\) lies in the separated recovery regime when it satisfies:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Structural model.)} The published VMW structural model conditions.
\item \textbf{(Anchor normalization.)} The first target-proxy coordinate satisfies \(X_1=1\) almost surely.
\item \textbf{(Finite regularity.)} The published VMW finite-regularity condition.
\item \textbf{(Spectral separation.)} The latent-class treatment effects satisfy \(\tau_u\ne\tau_v\) whenever \(u\ne v\).
\end{itemize}
In this regime, the separated-recovery estimator analyzed by \citet{VirkMazaheriWu2026} is evaluated under its stated sample-size and radius conditions and returns simultaneous high-probability bounds for the treatment effects, the anchor-normalized feature matrix, and the simplex-projected mixture weights.

blocks.title: Published converse transfer
blocks.body:
Fix \(k=d_x=d_z=2\), \(L=2\), and \(\sigma_0=1/10\).  There exist constants \(a,c\in\mathbb R\) such that
\[
0<a\le \frac18,
\qquad
0<c .
\]
For every \(n\ge 1\), the following hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Quotient witness pair.)} The two laws \(P_0^{\mathrm{wit}}\) and \(P_{a/\sqrt n}^{\mathrm{wit}}\) from \cref{obj:def:two-class-witness} belong to the published VMW model and satisfy VMW Assumption 4, while \(P_0^{\mathrm{wit}}\) lies outside the published separated recovery regime.
\item \textbf{(Quotient lower bound.)} For every class \(\mathcal V_n^\nu\) of full-data probability laws such that every \(P\in\mathcal V_n^\nu\) belongs to the published VMW model and satisfies VMW Assumption 4, if \(\mathcal V_n^\nu\) contains laws equal to \(P_0^{\mathrm{wit}}\) and \(P_{a/\sqrt n}^{\mathrm{wit}}\), then every estimator \(\widetilde\nu_n\) of the quotient effect law with support radius \(4\cdot 2\sqrt2/(1/10)\) has worst-case risk at least \(c/\sqrt n\):
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal V_n^\nu}
E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\!\left[
W_1\!\left(\widetilde\nu_n,\nu_P\right)
\right]
\ge \frac{c}{\sqrt n}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Separated labeled path.)} For every \(g\) in the gap-scale domain, define
\[
h(n,g):=\operatorname{calibratedDisplacement}(a,n,g).
\]
Then \(h(n,g)\) is in the tangent-amplitude domain, and the endpoint laws \(P_{g,0}\) and \(P_{g,h(n,g)}\) both belong to the published VMW model, satisfy VMW Assumption 4, and have spectrally separated latent effects.
\item \textbf{(Labeled-weight lower bound.)} For every \(g\) in the gap-scale domain and every class \(\mathcal V_{n,g}^p\) of full-data probability laws such that every \(P\in\mathcal V_{n,g}^p\) belongs to the published VMW model and satisfies VMW Assumption 4, if \(\mathcal V_{n,g}^p\) contains laws equal to \(P_{g,0}\) and \(P_{g,h(n,g)}\), then every estimator \(\widetilde p_n\) of the ordered latent weights satisfies
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal V_{n,g}^p}
E_{Q_P^{(n)}}\!\left[
\left\|\widetilde p_n-p^{\uparrow}(P)\right\|_1
\right]
\ge
c\min\{1,(\sqrt n\,g)^{-1}\}.
\]
\end{itemize}

cited_dependencies.statement: In the published VMW model, Assumption 1 includes \(Z\perp(X,Y)\mid(T,U)\), \(X\perp(Y,T)\mid U\), causal consistency \(Y=Y(T)\), and latent ignorability \(Y(t)\perp T\mid U\).  Assumption 2 requires \(A_0,A_1,B\) to have full column rank \(k\), and Section 4.2 uses strict latent positivity \(P(T=t\mid U=u)>0\).  These are qualitative conditions: the source does not impose the fixed margins \(\pi_0\) and \(\sigma_0\) used to define \(\mathcal M\).

cited_dependencies.locator: Assumption 3, lines 261--263; Assumption 4, lines 321--337; and Theorem 7.2, lines 350--381 of arXiv:2607.10926v1
cited_dependencies.statement: For fixed \(k,d_x,d_z\) and a population law \(P\), write \(M_{ZX\mid t}(P):=E_P[ZX^\top\mid T=t]\), \(M_{\mathrm{stack}}(P):=[M_{ZX\mid 0}(P)^\top,M_{ZX\mid 1}(P)^\top]^\top\), and let \(V_k(P)\) be an orthonormal basis for the population \(k\)-dimensional right singular subspace of \(M_{\mathrm{stack}}(P)\).  VMW Assumption 4 is the law-level requirement that there exist finite positive constants \(L_X,L_{ZX},L_{ZXY}\) for which \(\lVert X\rVert_2\le L_X\), \(\lVert ZX^\top\rVert_2\le L_{ZX}\), and \(\lVert YZX^\top\rVert_2\le L_{ZXY}\) almost surely under \(P\), while \(\pi(P):=\min_{t\in\{0,1\}}P(T=t)>0\) and \(\sigma(P):=\min\{\sigma_k(M_{\mathrm{stack}}(P)),\min_{t\in\{0,1\}}\sigma_k(M_{ZX\mid t}(P)V_k(P))\}>0\).  It subsequently defines \(M_X,M_Y,\kappa_B,\Gamma_X,\Gamma_Y\), and \(\kappa_{ZX}^{\star}\) as fixed derived conditioning quantities, not as additional conjunctive assumptions.  VMW Theorem 7.2 operates under the standing Assumption 1 conditions \(Z\perp(X,Y)\mid(T,U)\), \(X\perp(Y,T)\mid U\), causal consistency \(Y=Y(T)\), and latent ignorability \(Y(t)\perp T\mid U\), together with the anchor normalization \(X_1=1\) almost surely.  It additionally assumes Assumption 2, strict latent positivity, Assumption 4, and spectral separation, where spectral separation means \(\tau(u)\ne\tau(v)\) for distinct \(u,v\in\{1,\ldots,k\}\) and is vacuous for \(k=1\).  Together with its stated \(n,\eta\)-dependent sample-size and radius conditions, the theorem gives simultaneous high-probability finite-sample recovery of the treatment effects, the anchor-normalized feature matrix, and the simplex-projected mixture weights.  Consequently, when \(k\ge2\), a treatment-effect collision lies outside the separated recovery regime of VMW Theorem 7.2.

blocks.title: Sharp summary-inversion computation
blocks.body:
It remains open whether, in the fixed-dimensional exact-real model, one can compute exactly and in time polynomial in \(n\) the sharp summary-inversion image
\[
\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}
=
\{\overline F(q):q\in\mathcal K,\ d_S(q,\Pi(\widehat S_n))\le 2r_{n,\alpha}\}
\]
together with its exact support-dependent cluster extrema, using neither compact nearest-summary optimization nor black-box evaluation of \(\overline F\). The positive real law estimator \(\widehat\lambda_n\), the honest outer set \(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{alg}}_{n,\alpha}\), and every interval in the report \(\mathfrak R_{n,\alpha}\) have explicit fixed-dimensional constrained representations, including cases in which the raw empirical operator has nonreal eigenpairs. The question concerns a sharp polynomial-time algorithm for the original summary-inversion image and its extrema.

blocks.title: Compact loss selector
blocks.body:
For every \(d\in\mathbb N\), every set \(\mathcal K\subseteq \mathbb R^d\), and every loss \(d_S:\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\), suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Nonempty feasible set.)} \(\mathcal K\) is nonempty.
\item \textbf{(Compact feasible set.)} \(\mathcal K\) is compact.
\item \textbf{(Continuous loss.)} The map \((s,q)\mapsto d_S(s,q)\) is continuous.
\end{itemize}
Then there exists a Borel measurable map \(\Pi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d\) such that, for every \(s\in\mathbb R^d\),
\[
\Pi(s)\in\mathcal K
\quad\text{and}\quad
d_S(s,\Pi(s))\le d_S(s,q)\ \text{for every }q\in\mathcal K .
\]

blocks.title: Arm mass lower bound
blocks.body:
Let \(P\) be a full-data probability law in the setting of \cref{obj:def:model-class}. Suppose \(P\) satisfies \cref{obj:ass:latent-arm-positivity} with margin \(\pi_0\). Then, for each treatment arm \(t\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
k\pi_0 \le P(T=t).
\]

blocks.title: Observed proxy moment factorization
blocks.body:
Let \(P\) be a full-data probability law carrying \((U,T,X,Z,Y(0),Y(1),Y)\), with fixed target- and reference-proxy dimensions \(d_x,d_z\), in the uniformly conditioned proxy causal model class \(\mathcal M\) of \cref{obj:def:model-class}. Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Latent cardinality.)} The number \(k\) of latent classes satisfies \(2\le k\).
\item \textbf{(Target dimension.)} The target-proxy dimension satisfies \(k\le d_x\).
\item \textbf{(Boundedness radius.)} The uniform boundedness radius satisfies \(1\le L\), with the bounded-target-proxy condition as in \cref{obj:ass:bounded-x}.
\item \textbf{(Latent-arm margin.)} The latent-arm positivity margin satisfies \(\pi_0>0\), with latent-arm positivity as in \cref{obj:ass:latent-arm-positivity}.
\item \textbf{(Proxy separation.)} The reference- and target-proxy separation conditions hold as in \cref{obj:ass:reference-proxy-separation,obj:ass:target-proxy-separation}.
\end{itemize}
Then, for each treatment arm \(t\in\{0,1\}\), the observable armwise proxy moment \(M_t(P)\) from \cref{obj:def:observable-population-moments} factors as
\[
M_t(P)=A_t\Gamma_t B^\top,
\]
where \(A_t\) is the reference-proxy feature matrix of \cref{obj:def:reference-feature}, \(B\) is the target-proxy feature matrix of \cref{obj:def:target-feature}, and
\[
\Gamma_t
=
\operatorname{diag}\left\{
\frac{P(U=u,T=t)}{P(T=t)}:1\le u\le k
\right\}.
\]

blocks.title: Coordinate envelope bounds
blocks.body:
Let \(P\in\mathcal M\) be a full-data probability law carrying \((U,T,X,Z,Y(0),Y(1),Y)\), with \(\mathcal M\) as in \cref{obj:def:model-class}.  Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Latent cardinality.)} \(2\le k\).
\item \textbf{(Target-proxy dimension.)} \(k\le d_x\).
\item \textbf{(Envelope conditions.)} \(P\) satisfies \cref{obj:ass:bounded-x,obj:ass:bounded-proxy-product,obj:ass:bounded-outcome-proxy-product}.
\item \textbf{(Anchor normalization.)} \(P\) satisfies \cref{obj:ass:anchor}.
\end{itemize}
Then the model envelope \(L\) bounds the target proxy, the reference proxy, and the outcome--reference-proxy products \(P\)-almost surely:
\[
\Pr_P\{\,|X_i|\le L\text{ for every }1\le i\le d_x\,\}=1,
\]
\[
\Pr_P\{\,|Z_j|\le L\text{ for every }1\le j\le d_z\,\}=1,
\]
and
\[
\Pr_P\{\,|Y Z_j|\le L\text{ for every }1\le j\le d_z\,\}=1.
\]

blocks.title: Latent mean envelope
blocks.body:
Let \(P\in\mathcal M\) be a full-data probability law carrying \((U,T,X,Z,Y(0),Y(1),Y)\), as in \cref{obj:def:model-class}.  Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Latent cardinality.)} \(2\le k\).
\item \textbf{(Proxy dimensions.)} \(k\le d_x\) and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Model constants.)} \(1\le L\), \(\pi_0>0\), and \(\sigma_0>0\).
\item \textbf{(Model components.)} The model class includes the bounded target-proxy condition of \cref{obj:ass:bounded-x}, the latent-arm positivity condition of \cref{obj:ass:latent-arm-positivity}, and the proxy-rank margin condition of \cref{obj:ass:proxy-rank-margin}.
\end{itemize}
Then, for every latent class \(u\in\{1,\ldots,k\}\) and every treatment state \(t\in\{0,1\}\), the latent conditional potential-outcome mean \(\mu_{tu}\) of \cref{obj:def:latent-mean} satisfies
\[
|\mu_{tu}|\le \frac{L_\tau}{2},
\]
where \(L_\tau=4L\sqrt{d_z}/\sigma_0\) is the derived effect-support radius from \cref{obj:def:effect-radius}.

blocks.title: Latent effect envelope
blocks.body:
Let \(k,d_x,d_z\in\mathbb N\), let \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\), let \(P\) be a full-data probability law carrying \((U,T,X,Z,Y(0),Y(1),Y)\), and fix a latent class \(u\in\{1,\ldots,k\}\). Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimensions.)} \(2\le k\), \(k\le d_x\), and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Margins.)} \(1\le L\), \(\pi_0>0\), and \(\sigma_0>0\).
\item \textbf{(Model membership.)} \(P\in\mathcal M\) for the parameters \((k,d_x,d_z,L,\pi_0,\sigma_0)\), as in \cref{obj:def:model-class}, with the bounded-proxy, latent-arm-positivity, and proxy-rank-margin components recorded in \cref{obj:ass:bounded-x,obj:ass:latent-arm-positivity,obj:ass:proxy-rank-margin}.
\end{itemize}
Then the latent-class treatment effect \(\tau_u\), formed from the latent means in \cref{obj:def:latent-mean,obj:def:latent-effect}, satisfies
\[
|\tau_u|\le L_\tau=\frac{4L\sqrt{d_z}}{\sigma_0},
\]
where \(L_\tau\) is the derived effect-support radius in \cref{obj:def:effect-radius}.

blocks.title: Witness latent masses
blocks.body:
For every collision-witness effect displacement \(\varepsilon\in\mathbb R\) with \(0\le \varepsilon\le 1/8\), let \(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}\) be the two-class witness law of \cref{obj:def:two-class-witness}.  The latent-class masses \(p_u:=P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}(U=u)\) from \cref{obj:def:latent-mass} are
\[
p_1=\frac25,
\qquad
p_2=\frac35 .
\]
Equivalently, these masses are constant in \(\varepsilon\) over this range and are distinct.

blocks.title: Witness latent effects
blocks.body:
For every collision-witness effect displacement \(\varepsilon\in\mathbb R\) with \(0\le \varepsilon\le 1/8\) and every latent class \(u\in\{1,2\}\), the latent-class treatment effect \(\tau_u\) from \cref{obj:def:latent-effect} under the two-class Bernoulli witness law \(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}\) from \cref{obj:def:two-class-witness} is
\[
\tau_u(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}})
=
\begin{cases}
\frac14-\varepsilon, & u=1,\\
\frac14+\varepsilon, & u=2.
\end{cases}
\]

blocks.title: Observed arm mass
blocks.body:
For any collision-witness effect displacement \(\varepsilon\) and any treatment arm \(t\in\{0,1\}\), suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Lower bound.)} \(0\le \varepsilon\).
\item \textbf{(Upper bound.)} \(\varepsilon\le 1/8\).
\end{itemize}
For the two-class Bernoulli proxy witness law \(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}\) from \cref{obj:def:two-class-witness}, its observed-data marginal from \cref{obj:def:observed-margin} satisfies
\[
(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}})_O(T=t)
=
\begin{cases}
12/25, & t=0,\\
13/25, & t=1.
\end{cases}
\]

blocks.title: Witness feature determinant
blocks.body:
For every collision-witness effect displacement \(\varepsilon\in\mathbb R\) satisfying \(0\le \varepsilon\le 1/8\), let \(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}\) be the two-class Bernoulli proxy witness law from \cref{obj:def:two-class-witness}, and let \(B\) be its target-proxy feature matrix from \cref{obj:def:target-feature}. Then
\[
B_{00}B_{11}-B_{01}B_{10}=\frac35 .
\]

blocks.title: Witness reference-feature determinant
blocks.body:
For the two-class Bernoulli witness law \(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}\) and the reference-proxy feature matrix \(A_t\) in \cref{obj:def:two-class-witness,obj:def:reference-feature}, suppose
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Perturbation range.)} The collision-witness effect displacement \(\varepsilon\) satisfies \(0\le \varepsilon\le 1/8\).
\item \textbf{(Arm.)} The treatment arm \(t\) is binary, \(t\in\{0,1\}\).
\end{itemize}
Then
\[
\det(A_t)=\frac25 .
\]

blocks.title: Path proxy-rank margin
Path model membership
blocks.body:
Let \(g,h\in\mathbb R\). Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Gap range.)} \(0\le g\le 1/4\).
\item \textbf{(Path displacement.)} \(|h|\le 1/100\).
\end{itemize}
Then the path law \(P_{g,h}\) of \cref{obj:def:path-law-family} belongs to the uniformly conditioned model class \(\mathcal M\) of \cref{obj:def:model-class} with
\[
k=d_x=d_z=2,\qquad L=2,\qquad \pi_0=1/10,\qquad \sigma_0=1/10 .
\]
