Equivalently, \(P_{g,h}\) satisfies the core numerical domain for \(k=d_x=d_z=2\), together with \cref{obj:ass:reference-proxy-separation,obj:ass:target-proxy-separation,obj:ass:consistency,obj:ass:latent-ignorability,obj:ass:anchor,obj:ass:bounded-x,obj:ass:bounded-proxy-product,obj:ass:bounded-outcome-proxy-product,obj:ass:latent-arm-positivity,obj:ass:proxy-rank-margin}, using latent-arm positivity margin \(1/10\) and proxy-rank margin \(1/10\).

blocks.title: Path stratum membership
blocks.body:
For real numbers \(g\) and \(h\), suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Gap scale.)} The local effect-gap scale satisfies \(0<g\le 1/4\).
\item \textbf{(Path displacement.)} The path displacement satisfies \(|h|\le 1/100\).
\end{itemize}
Then the path law \(P_{g,h}\) of \cref{obj:def:path-law-family} belongs to the gap-local stratum \(\mathcal M(g)\) of \cref{obj:def:gap-stratum}, with \(L=2\), \(\pi_0=1/10\), and \(\sigma_0=1/10\). Equivalently, \(P_{g,h}\in\mathcal M\) as specified by \cref{obj:def:model-class,obj:ass:bounded-x,obj:ass:latent-arm-positivity,obj:ass:proxy-rank-margin}, its smallest positive effect gap \(\delta(P_{g,h})\) from \cref{obj:def:effect-gap} satisfies the gap window of \cref{obj:ass:gap-window},
\[
\frac{g}{2}\le \delta(P_{g,h})\le 2g,
\]
and its latent effects from \cref{obj:def:latent-effect} are distinct as in \cref{obj:ass:distinct-effects}.

blocks.title: Path local weight membership
blocks.body:
Let \(n\in\mathbb N\), let \(c_{\mathrm{loc}}\in\mathbb R\) be the local Kullback--Leibler radius constant, and let \(g,h\in\mathbb R\). Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Local radius.)} \(0<c_{\mathrm{loc}}<1\), as in \cref{obj:def:local-kl-radius}.
\item \textbf{(Gap scale.)} The local effect-gap scale \(g\) is in the gap window of \cref{obj:ass:gap-window}, with \(0<g\le 1/4\).
\item \textbf{(Path displacement.)} The path displacement satisfies \(|h|\le 1/100\).
\item \textbf{(Observed KL calibration.)}
\[
16000\,g^2h^2\le \frac{c_{\mathrm{loc}}}{n}.
\]
\end{itemize}
Then the path law \(P_{g,h}\) from \cref{obj:def:path-law-family} belongs to the local labeled-weight experiment \(\mathcal L_{n,g}^p\) of \cref{obj:def:local-weight-experiment} with \(L=2\), \(\pi_0=1/10\), and \(\sigma_0=1/10\). Equivalently, \(P_{g,h}\in\mathcal M(g)\) as in \cref{obj:def:gap-stratum}, and its observed-data marginal from \cref{obj:def:observed-margin} obeys the neighborhood condition of \cref{obj:ass:local-weight-neighborhood}:
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left((P_{g,h})_O\,\Vert\,(P_{g,0})_O\right)
\le \frac{c_{\mathrm{loc}}}{n},
\qquad
P_{g,0}=P^{\mathrm{wit}}_{g/2}.
\]

blocks.title: Ordered aggregate mass map
blocks.body:
For a labelled representative \(\xi=\sum_{i=1}^k w_i\delta_{x_i}\in\mathcal P_{\le k}([-L_\tau,L_\tau])\), define \(\operatorname{orderedMasses}(\xi)\in\mathbb R^k\) as follows. If every labelled weight is positive and the labelled atoms are distinct, then its \(j\)th coordinate is the mass of the atom whose support rank is \(j\):
\[
\operatorname{orderedMasses}(\xi)_j
:=\sum_{i=1}^k w_i\mathbf 1\!\left\{\#\{\ell:x_\ell<x_i\}=j\right\},
\qquad j=0,\ldots,k-1.
\]
If some labelled weight is zero or two labelled atoms coincide, set \(\operatorname{orderedMasses}(\xi):=(1/k,\ldots,1/k)\).

blocks.title: Ordered masses are representative-invariant
blocks.body:
Fix \(k\in\mathbb N\) and a real support radius.  Let \(\nu\) and \(\xi\) be valid labelled atomic representatives with \(k\) slots in the corresponding compact interval, as in \cref{obj:def:atomic-law-class}.  If \(\nu\) and \(\xi\) represent the same aggregated probability measure, then their ordered-mass vectors coincide:
\[
\operatorname{orderedMasses}(\nu)=\operatorname{orderedMasses}(\xi).
\]

blocks.title: Outcome proxy moment factorization
blocks.body:
Let \(P\), a full-data probability law carrying \((U,T,X,Z,Y(0),Y(1),Y)\), belong to the model class \(\mathcal M\) in \cref{obj:def:model-class}. Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Latent classes.)} \(2\le k\).
\item \textbf{(Positivity margin.)} The latent-arm positivity margin satisfies \(\pi_0>0\).
\item \textbf{(Model conditions.)} The reference- and target-proxy separation, consistency, latent ignorability, latent-arm positivity, bounded outcome-proxy product, and bounded target-proxy conditions in \cref{obj:ass:reference-proxy-separation,obj:ass:target-proxy-separation,obj:ass:consistency,obj:ass:latent-ignorability,obj:ass:latent-arm-positivity,obj:ass:bounded-outcome-proxy-product,obj:ass:bounded-x} hold.
\end{itemize}
Then, for each treatment arm \(t\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
N_t(P)
=
A_t\,\Gamma_t\,\operatorname{diag}\{\mu_{tu}:1\le u\le k\}\,B^\top,
\qquad
\Gamma_t
=
\operatorname{diag}\left\{\frac{P(U=u,T=t)}{P(T=t)}:1\le u\le k\right\}.
\]
Here \(N_t(P)\) is the observable armwise \(YZX^\top\) population moment in \cref{obj:def:observable-population-moments}, \(A_t\) is the reference-proxy feature matrix in \cref{obj:def:reference-feature}, \(B\) is the target-proxy feature matrix in \cref{obj:def:target-feature}, and \(\mu_{tu}\) is the latent conditional potential-outcome mean in \cref{obj:def:latent-mean}.

blocks.title: Latent-arm weight injectivity
Moore--Penrose product cancellation
blocks.body:
Let \(C\in\mathbb R^{\mathrm{rows}\times r}\), \(B\in\mathbb R^{\mathrm{cols}\times r}\), and \(\mu\in\mathbb R^r\). Suppose that the linear maps represented by \(C\) and by \(B\), each with domain \(\mathbb R^r\), are injective. Then
\[
(CB^\top)^\dagger\bigl(C\operatorname{diag}(\mu)B^\top\bigr)
=
(B^\dagger)^\top \operatorname{diag}(\mu)B^\top .
\]

blocks.title: Attaining KR potential
blocks.body:
Let \(\nu\) and \(\xi\) be valid represented atomic laws with finite labelled slot sets: their weights are nonnegative and sum to one.  Let \(\varphi_{\nu,\xi}\) be the cumulative-distribution-gap sign Kantorovich--Rubinstein potential selected for the pair \((\nu,\xi)\).  Then \(\varphi_{\nu,\xi}\) is one-Lipschitz, is normalized by
\[
\varphi_{\nu,\xi}(0)=0,
\]
and attains the Wasserstein distance of \cref{obj:def:wasserstein-distance}:
\[
W_1(\nu,\xi)
=
\left|
  \int \varphi_{\nu,\xi}\,d\nu
  -
  \int \varphi_{\nu,\xi}\,d\xi
\right|.
\]
Moreover, for every \(\epsilon\in\mathbb R\), if every one-Lipschitz function \(\varphi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) satisfying \(\varphi(0)=0\) obeys
\[
\left|
  \int \varphi\,d\nu
  -
  \int \varphi\,d\xi
\right|
\le \epsilon,
\]
then
\[
W_1(\nu,\xi)\le \epsilon.
\]

blocks.title: Coordinate metric comparison
blocks.body:
Let \(d_x\) and \(d_z\) be fixed target- and reference-proxy dimensions, and let \(s,s'\) be elements of the five-block observable summary space in \cref{obj:def:observable-summary}. Equip this space with its coordinate Euclidean distance \(\rho_{\mathrm{sum}}\). Then
\[
d_S(s,s')
\le
\bigl(4\operatorname{Ent}_{d_z,d_x}+d_x\bigr)\rho_{\mathrm{sum}}(s,s'),
\]
where
\[
\operatorname{Ent}_{r,c}
:=
c\,r\,\|J_c\|_{\mathrm{op}},
\]
and \(J_c:\mathbb R^c\to(\{1,\ldots,c\}\to\mathbb R)\) is the canonical coordinate identification.

blocks.title: Summary metric continuity
blocks.body:
For fixed target- and reference-proxy dimensions \(d_x,d_z\), let \(d_S\) be the summary metric on observable moment summaries from \cref{obj:def:observable-summary}. The map
\[
(s,q)\longmapsto d_S(s,q)
\]
from the product of the five-block summary space with itself to \(\mathbb R\) is continuous.

blocks.title: Stacked proxy signal margin
blocks.body:
Let \(P\), a full-data probability law carrying \((U,T,X,Z,Y(0),Y(1),Y)\), belong to the uniformly conditioned proxy causal model class \(\mathcal M\) in \cref{obj:def:model-class}. Suppose:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimensions.)} \(2\le k\le d_x\), where \(k\) is the number of latent classes and \(d_x\) is the target-proxy dimension.
\item \textbf{(Radius.)} \(L\ge 1\), with the bounded target-proxy condition in \cref{obj:ass:bounded-x}.
\item \textbf{(Margins.)} \(\pi_0>0\) and \(\sigma_0>0\), with the latent-arm positivity and proxy-rank margin conditions in \cref{obj:ass:latent-arm-positivity,obj:ass:proxy-rank-margin}.
\end{itemize}
Then the vertically stacked observable proxy moment satisfies
\[
\pi_0\sigma_0^2
\le
\sigma_{k-1}\!\left\{\operatorname{stack}\bigl(M_0(P),M_1(P)\bigr)\right\},
\]
where \(\sigma_{k-1}\) uses zero-based singular-value indexing and \(M_0(P),M_1(P)\) are the armwise \(ZX^\top\) population moments from \cref{obj:def:observable-population-moments}.

blocks.title: Compressed spectral certificate
blocks.body:
Let \(k,d_x,d_z\in\mathbb N\), let \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\in\mathbb R\), and let \(Q\) be a full-data probability law in the uniformly conditioned model class \(\mathcal M\) of \cref{obj:def:model-class}, with observable summary \(S(Q)\) as in \cref{obj:def:observable-summary}. Assume that \(Q\) satisfies \cref{obj:ass:anchor,obj:ass:proxy-rank-margin,obj:ass:latent-arm-positivity}. Let \(M_t(S(Q))\) be the \(t\)-arm \(ZX^\top\) moment block from \cref{obj:def:observable-population-moments}, and set
\[
G:=\operatorname{stack}(M_0(S(Q)),M_1(S(Q))).
\]
Then there exist a signal basis \(V\) spanning the signal row space of \(S(Q)\) and a real diagonalization of the compressed effect operator \(\Delta Q(Q)\) from \cref{obj:def:compressed-operator} such that:
\begin{enumerate}
\item for each arm \(t\in\{0,1\}\), the compressed map
\[
x\longmapsto M_t(S(Q))Vx
\]
is injective;
\item the stacked proxy moment has rank
\[
\operatorname{rank}(G)=k;
\]
\item for every index \(j\),
\[
\frac{\pi_0\sigma_0^2}{2}\le \sigma_j(G)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
j<k;
\]
\item the eigenvalue vector of the diagonalization is the latent-effect vector \((\tau_u(Q))_u\) from \cref{obj:def:latent-effect};
\item writing \(R\) for the diagonalizing basis matrix, the left and right spectral anchors satisfy
\[
a(Q)=R^{-\top}p(Q),
\qquad
R^{-1}c(Q)=\mathbf 1_k,
\]
where \(p(Q)=(p_u(Q))_u\) is the latent-mass vector from \cref{obj:def:latent-mass}.
\end{enumerate}

blocks.title: Diagonalization condition bound
blocks.body:
Let \(d_x\ge 1\) and \(k\ge 1\).  Let \(B\in\mathbb R^{d_x\times k}\), and let \(F\) be a thin signal factorization of \(B\), written \(B=V\Upsilon\), with coordinate inverse \(\Upsilon^{-1}\).  Let \(\tau\in\mathbb R^k\).  Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Feature bound.)} For a constant \(L\ge 0\) as in \cref{obj:ass:bounded-x}, \(|B_{iu}|\le L\) for every row \(i\) and latent index \(u\).
\item \textbf{(Coordinate-inverse bound.)} For a constant \(\sigma_0>0\) as in \cref{obj:ass:proxy-rank-margin}, \(|(\Upsilon^{-1})_{ru}|\le \sigma_0^{-1}\) for every pair of coordinate indices \(r,u\).
\end{itemize}
Define
\[
K_{\mathrm{forw}}
:=
\operatorname{Ent}_{d_x,k}\operatorname{Ent}_{k,k}\operatorname{Ent}_{k,d_x}\sigma_0^{-1}
+
\bigl(\operatorname{Ent}_{d_x,d_x}
+
\operatorname{Ent}_{d_x,k}\operatorname{Ent}_{k,d_x}\bigr),
\]
\[
K_{\mathrm{back}}
:=
\operatorname{Ent}_{d_x,k}\operatorname{Ent}_{k,k}\operatorname{Ent}_{k,d_x}(d_xL)
+
\bigl(\operatorname{Ent}_{d_x,d_x}
+
\operatorname{Ent}_{d_x,k}\operatorname{Ent}_{k,d_x}\bigr),
\]
and
\[
\kappa_\star
:=
\operatorname{Ent}_{d_x,d_x}^{\,2}K_{\mathrm{forw}}K_{\mathrm{back}},
\]
where \(\operatorname{Ent}_{r,c}\) is the entrywise-to-operator norm constant of \cref{obj:lem:summary-metric-coordinate-comparison}.  Then the real diagonalization associated with \(F\) and \(\tau\) has condition number at most \(\kappa_\star\).

blocks.title: Constructive repair handle \(m\)
blocks.body:
The constructive repair handle is defined for laws in \cref{obj:def:model-class} as follows.
\begin{enumerate}
\item At the realized empirical summary, define the first \(2k\) spectral moments by
\[
m=(m_j)_{0\le j<2k}.
\]
\item Among all valid positive \(k\)-atomic laws \(\sum_i w_i\delta_{x_i}\), choose a minimizer of
\[
\sum_{j=0}^{2k-1}\left|m_j-\sum_i w_i x_i^j\right|.
\]
\item Extract the repaired real probability measure from the minimizing positive \(k\)-atomic law, transporting aggregate projector mass across each cluster diameter after replacing individual eigenvectors inside overlapping localization discs by Kato contour projectors.
\item For the labeled-weight converse, differentiate the Bernoulli factorization of \(P_{\varepsilon}^{\mathrm{wit}}\) and solve the linear score-cancellation equations for the proxy and treatment primitives so that a weight displacement \(h\) preserves the factorization and the observed score has order \(g h\).
\end{enumerate}

blocks.title: Finite-net program \(\operatorname{NetProgram}(A,\omega)\)
blocks.body:
The inputs are a stored representative library \(A=(A_i)_i\) and an observed sample \(\omega\).
\begin{enumerate}
\item For each representative \(A_i\), let \(S_i=(M_{0,i},M_{1,i},N_{0,i},N_{1,i},m_{X,i})\) be its stored five-block summary, and let
\[
\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}(i)
\]
be its position in the fixed lexicographic library order.

\item Define the spectral law attached to representative \(A_i\) by
\[
\lambda^{\mathrm{spec}}(A_i),
\]
the real atomic effect law returned by the thresholded exact-real spectral run for \(A_i\).

\item For the empirical five-block summary
\[
\widehat S_n(\omega)
=
(\widehat M_{0,n},\widehat M_{1,n},\widehat N_{0,n},\widehat N_{1,n},\widehat m_{X,n}),
\]
define the comparison criterion
\[
\Delta_i(\omega)
:=
\lVert M_{0,i}-\widehat M_{0,n}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
+
\lVert M_{1,i}-\widehat M_{1,n}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
+
\lVert N_{0,i}-\widehat N_{0,n}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
+
\lVert N_{1,i}-\widehat N_{1,n}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
+
\lVert m_{X,i}-\widehat m_{X,n}\rVert_2.
\]

\item If the library is nonempty, define the selected representative index by
\[
\widehat i(\omega)
\in
\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{i}
\bigl(\Delta_i(\omega),\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}(i)\bigr),
\]
with the minimum taken in lexicographic order.

\item The finite-library spectral program returns the selected representative and its spectral law,
\[
\operatorname{NetProgram}(A,\omega)
:=
\bigl(A_{\widehat i(\omega)},\lambda^{\mathrm{spec}}(A_{\widehat i(\omega)})\bigr),
\]
when the library is nonempty, and returns the canonical zero law when the library is empty. Its returned effect-law component is
\[
\operatorname{law}(\operatorname{NetProgram}(A,\omega)).
\]
\end{enumerate}

blocks.title: Finite-net estimator \(\widehat\nu_n^{\mathrm{net}}\)
blocks.body:
The input is the empirical summary \(\widehat S_n\); the tuning constants are
\[
D:=4d_zd_x+d_x,\qquad
b:=4\sqrt{d_zd_x}+\sqrt{d_x},\qquad
\epsilon_n:=n^{-1/2}.
\]
\begin{enumerate}
\item Partition the coordinate box \([-L,L]^D\) into a deterministic lexicographically ordered grid of half-open cubes whose side length is at most
\[
\epsilon_n/b.
\]

\item If \(\mathscr S=\varnothing\), set
\[
\widehat\nu_n^{\mathrm{net}}:=\delta_0
\]
and stop.

\item For each grid cube that intersects \(\mathscr S\), choose one representative
\[
q_{n,\ell}\in\mathscr S.
\]
Let \(\widehat q_n\) be the smallest-index minimizer
\[
\widehat q_n
\in
\arg\min_{\ell} d_S(q_{n,\ell},\widehat S_n).
\]

\item At \(\widehat q_n\), form the vertically stacked proxy moment and retain the \(k\) right singular directions whose singular values exceed \(\pi_0\sigma_0^2/2\). Denote the resulting orthonormal basis by
\[
V.
\]
Using this basis, form the compressed effect operator, left anchor, and right anchor
\[
\Delta,\qquad a,\qquad c
\]
from the compressed-operator formulas.

\item For each distinct eigenvalue \(\lambda\) of \(\Delta\), define the spectral projector
\[
E_\lambda
:=
\prod_{\gamma\in\operatorname{spec}(\Delta):\,\gamma\ne\lambda}
\frac{\Delta-\gamma I_k}{\lambda-\gamma},
\]
with the empty product equal to \(I_k\).

\item Output the atomic law
\[
\widehat\nu_n^{\mathrm{net}}
:=
\sum_{\lambda\in\operatorname{spec}(\Delta)}
a^\top E_\lambda c\,\delta_\lambda .
\]
\end{enumerate}

blocks.title: Polynomial finite-net estimator
blocks.body:
Fix integers \(k,d_x,d_z\) and real constants \(L,\pi_0,\sigma_0\). Suppose
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimensions.)} \(2\le k\), \(k\le d_x\), and \(k\le d_z\).
\item \textbf{(Bounds and margins.)} \(1\le L\), \(0<\pi_0\le (2k)^{-1}\), and \(0<\sigma_0\le 1\).
\end{itemize}
Then there are constants \(C_{\mathrm{mod}}>0\) and \(C>0\) such that, for every integer \(n\ge 1\), there is a class-dependent finite library \(A=(A_i)_i\) of representative summaries as in \cref{obj:def:finite-net-law-estimator} with the following properties. For every uniform provider of the fixed-parameter exact-real primitives on the admissible core parameter domain, the finite-net estimator \(\widehat\nu_n^{\mathrm{net}}\) is Borel measurable, and
\[
|A|\le C n^{(4d_zd_x+d_x)/2}.
\]
For every observed sample \(\omega=(O_1,\ldots,O_n)\in O_{d_x,d_z}^n\), the operation count of the same exact-real execution that returns \(\widehat\nu_n^{\mathrm{net}}(\omega)\) is at most
\[
C\{n+n^{(4d_zd_x+d_x)/2}\}.
\]
Its trace is exactly the empirical-summary trace, followed by the exhaustive finite-library search trace, and followed by the selected spectral-run trace when a representative is selected; if no representative is selected, the final spectral-run trace is empty.

If the program selects index \(i\) on sample \(\omega\), then \(S_i\) is a nearest library summary to the empirical summary \(\widehat S_n(\omega)\) of \cref{obj:def:empirical-summary}:
\[
d_S(S_i,\widehat S_n(\omega))\le d_S(S_j,\widehat S_n(\omega))
\qquad\text{for every }j.
\]
Among all tied nearest summaries, \(i\) has minimal lexicographic rank:
\[
d_S(S_i,\widehat S_n(\omega))=d_S(S_j,\widehat S_n(\omega))
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}(i)\le \operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{lex}}(j).
\]
For the exact spectral run at \(S_i\), the estimator equals the run's returned effect law. For each treatment value \(t\), the observed proxy moment at \(S_i\), multiplied by the run's basis matrix, defines an injective Euclidean linear map. The stacked proxy moment at \(S_i\) satisfies the exact threshold characterization
\[
\frac{\pi_0\sigma_0^2}{2}\le \sigma_j(\operatorname{stack}(M_0(S_i),M_1(S_i)))
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
j<k,
\]
for every singular-value index \(j\). Every eigenvalue of the compressed operator formed at \(S_i\) with the run's basis and spans appears among the eigenvalues returned by that run.

For every stored representative \(S_i\) and every rectangular perturbation \(H\in\mathbb R^{2d_z\times d_x}\),
\[
\|H\|_{\mathrm{op}}<\frac{\pi_0\sigma_0^2}{2}
\]
implies that singular-value thresholding at \(\pi_0\sigma_0^2/2\) recovers exactly the \(k\)-dimensional matrix signal space for
\[
\operatorname{stack}(M_0(S_i),M_1(S_i))+H.
\]
For every index \(i\), there is a model law \(Q\in\mathcal M\) from \cref{obj:def:model-class} whose observable summary is \(S_i\), and the exact spectral run at \(S_i\) returns the quotient law \(\nu_Q\). Each returned representative effect law is a valid atomic law.

For every \(P\in\mathcal M\), every observed sample \(\omega\in O_{d_x,d_z}^n\) satisfies
\[
W_1\!\left(\widehat\nu_n^{\mathrm{net}}(\omega),\nu_P\right)
\le
C_{\mathrm{mod}}\left\{2d_S(\widehat S_n(\omega),S(P))+n^{-1/2}\right\}.
\]
Finally, for every tail level \(\eta\) with \(0<\eta<1/2\) and every \(P\in\mathcal M\),
\[
Q_P^{(n)}\!\left(
W_1\!\left(\widehat\nu_n^{\mathrm{net}},\nu_P\right)
>
C\sqrt{\frac{\log(C/\eta)}{n}}
\right)
\le \eta .
\]
